3.9 Revision of norms for checking and re-sealing of HT & LT connections
by operation and M&P wing. (Sales Circular No. U- 38/2021)

Please refer to Sales Circular No. U-24/2003 dated 11.07.2003 & U-04/2004 dated
12.01.2004 vide which norms for checking and re-sealing of HT & LT connections by
operation and M&P wing has been circulated.
  The matter has been re-considered and the following has been decided: -
1. For eliminating any lapses at the time of release of new connection, the provision of
M&P checking will be provided by SE (Monitoring) in online new connection software by
creating login-ids of SDOs (M&P) and XENs (M&P) in next 20 days. After implementation,
the intimation by SDO ‘OP’ to M&P wing for sealing along with M&P Performa will be done
through online software only and M&P wing is also required to upload MT1 report in
software only to close the case.
2. For the purpose, the area of XEN/M&P will be divided under all SDO (M&P) by
designation i.e. SDO (M&P-1), SDO (M&P-2) & SDO (M&P-3) etc. and against each SDO
(M&P) specific operation sub-divisions will be allocated and binded.
3. The connections of load from 0 to 20 KW will be released by SDO (Operations).
However, the connections where LT-CT meter is installed and requires sealing by M&P and
all LT connections of load upto 20 to 50 kW will be released by SDO ‘OP’ and concerned
SDO (M&P) shall try to reach on site at the same time otherwise re-seal the connection
within maximum time period of 3 days.
4. All HT connections above 50 kW must be released & re-sealed jointly by SDO
(Operation) & SDO/M&P. Such type of connections should not be released without M&P
wing under any circumstances. SDO/OP will upload the completely filled in detail the
Performa for release of new CT/PT connection on portal through his log id, which will
automatically reflected in the Login Id of SDO (M&P) & XEN (M&P) concerned.
5. SDO (M&P) will have to upload MT-1 report citing the site condition. The SDO/M&P
will have maximum time period of 2 days for checking the same connection and upload
MT1 report on the portal. Any pendency for more than 2 days on part of M&P wing will be
observed to be delayed in performance.
6. SE (M&P) shall ensure that all MT-1 report of periodical checking are made available
to Chief Auditor on the same day through E-mail and consolidated reports of complete
month by 7th of next month. SE (Monitoring) in next 2 months shall implement software for
online generation of MT1 Report of periodical checking and its availability to all office
through Log In id in Web-based Portal.
7. The site checking of HT and LT CT connections by M&P wing will be carried out as

312

per Supply Code Regulation (HT meter once in 6 months and LT CT meter – once in 3 years
or earlier). The checking report will be prepared by the concerned SDO/M&P in the
prescribed format at the time of checking and uploaded on the web portal.
8. Seasonal Industries such as Ice Factories, Ice Candies, Cold Storage units, Cotton
Ginning Mills and Rice Sellers shall be checked twice during the season i.e. at least once
every three months.
9. Since the load of Saw Mill used in plywood industry is not substantial, therefore it
may be treated as a part of plywood industry.
10. The connections of HT and LT CT consumers, who were involved in theft of energy
during the last 3 years, will be checked every 6 months.
11. The meter readings of HT (other than AMR facility) and LT, CT consumers will be
taken only through MRI/CMRI by (OP) staff. The officer/official taking reading will also
physically inspect the metering installation with regard to any visible irregularity. He will
also down load the tamper information data and the load survey data from CT meter. To
detect the slowness of the meter the officer/ official will check all the voltages and currents
in each phase of the meter and ensure that the status “P” does not persist in the meter. In
case he observes that any of the voltages/currents is missing in the meter and also status
“P” is displayed in the meter then he should immediately inform the concerned M & P Divn.
for suitable action. The SDO/OP incharge of S/Divn. shall be personally responsible to
ensure that the above data is obtained every month in respect of all HT and LT meters.
12. The SDO (OP) will send tamper information data, load survey data and the
consumption data of all HT/LT CT consumers to the concerned Xen/M&P by the 10th of the
month succeeding the month in which the meter readings have been taken. In case, the
above schedule is not adhered to, Xen/M&P will immediately report the same to the SE/OP
of the Circle and to SE/M&P for appropriate action against the SDO/OP.
13. The requirement of presence of M&P staff at the time of reconnection after TDCO
shall be done away with. However, the presence of M&P staff at the time of fault and at the
time of PDCO and resetting of MDI will continue. New connection will be released after
checking by M&P staff as per the existing practice.
14. The responsibility for making proper and accurate analysis shall rest with the
SDO/M&P in respect of connections upto 500KW and Xen/M&P in respect of connections
have 500 KW. In case, theft of energy is detected later at any premises having HT or LT CT
connection and it can be shown that such theft could have been detected through analysis
of data down loaded from the meter, the Xen/M&P or SDO/M&P, as the case maybe, shall
be held accountable for failure to analyze the same from the data available.
15. Technical audit of 33KV sub-stations, checking of feeder meters at sub-stations as
well as joint checking of inter utility meters alongwith HVPN staff, shall continue as earlier.

 Sales Circular No. U-24/2003 & U-04/2004 stands superseded.

3.10 Release of electricity connections to Electric Vehicle Charging Stations.
(Sales Circular No. U-30/2021)

To address the regulatory complication of “One Connection in One Premises” mentioned in
Clause 3.8 of HERC (Duty to Supply Electricity on request and Power to Recover

313

Expenditure and Power to Recover Security) Regulations, 2016 (S/C No. U-09/2020) while
releasing electricity connections to Electric Vehicle Charging Stations, the Hon’ble
Commission has decided in its order dated 05.08.2021 in case No. PRO-17 of 2021 as
under:-
a) Tariff applicable for charging of Electric Vehicle at premises other than charging
stations shall be the same as applicable for the relevant category of connection at such
premises.
b) Tariff for Electric Vehicle (EV) charging stations on single point delivery shall be
applicable for charging of batteries at swapping facilities provided that such swapping
facilities are exclusively used for swapping of batteries of E-Rickshaw/E-Vehicle only.
c) At EV Charging station a separate electricity connection shall be taken by the
applicant for other associated purposes such as office of charging station, public amenities,
consumption of other equipment etc. The applicant shall ensure a separate metering
arrangement for such purposes and tariff as applicable to relevant category shall be
applicable to the same.
d) Permit a separate connection for EV charging in retails outlets of Oil Marketing
Companies, Housing Societies, Malls, Office Complexes, restaurants, Hotels, Parking of
Metro Stations or its premises etc.
e) Further, in cases where single point connection has been provided in the premises,
and a separate EV connection is desired at LT level, Distribution Licensee in such cases
may adopt minus metering by providing separate wiring and metering for EV charging
activities.
f) Applicant must be having the approval for safety and/or fire clearance for EV
Charging station wherever applicable from the concerned department such as petroleum
and Explosives Safety Organization (PESO), Fire Department, etc.
  Sales Circular No. U-09/2020 stands amended to the above extent only.
  The above instructions should be brought to notice of all concerned for
meticulous compliance.

3.11 Self-declaration for consumer electrical installation upto 50 KW for all
categories of consumers. (Sales Circular No. U- 07/2021).

 In spirit of Ease of Doing Business to facilitate an early release of connection,
following guidelines are hereby specified w.r.t. the inspection of premises of consumers for
release of connection by superseding completely Sales Instruction No. U-07/2007 dated
01.02.2007.
(a) The applicants with applied load upto 50 KW under low tension (LT) category is not
required to submit any test report from licensed contractor or any self-certification signed
document for the electrical installation of his premises.
(b) Instead of above, in the online application form under declaration by consumer,
additional clause ‘f’ will be provided, wherein the applicant will give following declaration: -
“That the internal wiring at the premises has been got executed and tested by a
Licensed Electrical Contractor/Designated Officer of the Govt. and test certificate is
available with the applicant”
(c) While releasing the connection, concerned JE incharge is not required to do any
physical inspection of the connected load or its verification.

314

(d) For the purpose of connected load, the same should be assessed through MDI reading
available in the meter which should be taken while taking monthly meter reading either
through manual mode or through downloading of data.
(e) For consumers with applied load greater than 50 KW on HT category, the inspection
report of electrical installation by Chief Electrical Inspector (CEI) is mandatory. However,
no test report is required to be submitted by the applicant to the SDO ’OP’ or any other
office and its verification by SDO ’OP’.
(f) For extension of load of existing HT consumers, the Chief Electrical Inspector (CEI)
inspection is only required when additional transformer is installed by him otherwise no
Chief Electrical Inspector (CEI) certification is required for extension of load.
(g) Existing HT consumers be intimated by SDO ’OP’ to undertake the annual inspection
from Chief Electrical Inspector (CEI) and compliance of the consumer be ensured.
(h) All SEs (OP) are requested to ensure vide publicity in the local newspaper/Cable TV
etc.
  Sales Instruction No. U-07/2007 stands superseded

Rated frequency of the alternating current system shall be 50 cycles per second. The voltage
and frequency shall be kept within the range as specified in the relevant rules / Regulations
made by the Govt. of India or the Central Electricity Authority from time to time.

load:

Contracted load exceeding 50 KW and up to 5000 kVA 3 Phase at 11 kV

at a voltage other than specified in Regulation 3.2.1/ approved plan, the licensee may accept
the request of the applicant with the approval of the Commission.
 Further, in case 33KV voltage level is not available in the area of supply than load
above 5 MVA upto 8 MVA may be served through 11 KV feeder with appropriate type/size of
conductor. Provided, the difference of cost of 33 KV substation at the consumer end along

bay and the actual cost of connection of 11 KV is borne by the consumer.
 Provided further that, in case intermediate voltage level between 33 KV and 220 KV is
not available in the area of supply of the licensee, the load upto 37.5 MVA may be served
through 33 KV feeder with appropriate type/ size of conductor provided the difference of cost
of substation as per Regulation 3.2.1 at the consumer end along with its connectivity from the
distribution / transmission licensee’s substation including the bay and the actual cost of
connection on 33 KV is borne by the consumer.

4.5  Procedure for Providing Temporary Supply (Clause from Sales Circular U-
02/2020)
4.5.1  Temporary supply shall be given for short-term requirements including construction,
dewatering, marriages, religious functions, cultural functions, exhibitions, touring
cinemas, theatres and circuses, provided that the said activity/premises is duly authorized
by thn;e competent authority, wherever required.
4.5.2  Temporary supply connection shall be granted for a period of up to 3 months at a
time, which can be further extended depending upon the requirement. For extension of the
period of temporary supply, the procedure detailed in Regulation 4.5.12 shall be applicable.
Provided that in case of construction of buildings (both residential and non-residential),
where it would take longer time for completion of the same or other such projects, the
temporary supply connection shall be given for a period as under:
For construction of buildings  =  Two years
For other projects    =  One year
The above period shall be extended by six months at a time on the request of the developer
if the project/building is not completed by that time.
Provided further that when any part of the building / project has been effectively completed
and possession offered to a prospective occupant, then the developer/occupant of such
building/portion shall apply for a permanent connection to the licensee within one month
from the date of such effective completion/offer of possession. The temporary connection
shall be removed three months after the date of such effective completion / offer of
possession.
4.5.10 After deposit of estimated cost and advance consumption charges for temporary
electricity connection by the applicant, and satisfactory testing of the consumer
installation, the temporary connection shall be released by the date of requirement as

One Connection in One Premises (Clause from Sales Circular No. 09/2020)
 (1)  A consumer shall be treated as a distinct entity and shall be deemed to be an
independent establishment, if
(a)  it is a separate unit in duly partitioned premises owned or taken on lease/rent;

320

(b)  there is a separate operative entrance and that the internal wiring of the premises
is separate;
(c)  it is registered as a separate entity/firm under the relevant law;
(d)  it holds a separate Sales Tax/VAT number and is independently assessed to Income
Tax;
(e)  the occupant shall submit an affidavit confirming that the power will be used only
for the premises for which the connection is sought and there will not be any cross supply.
(2)  In case a tenant requires a separate connection in the same premises, he shall
furnish an undertaking from the landlord duly witnessed by two neighbours stating that
the landlord shall clear all the liabilities in case the tenant leaves the premises without
paying the distribution licensee's dues.
(3)  If a portion of residential/industrial premises is regularly used for any commercial
activity permitted under law, the consumer shall be required to obtain a separate
connection under non domestic supply category for the portion put to commercial use. In
such an event, two connections, one under domestic supply schedule/industrial supply
schedule and the other under non domestic supply schedule shall be permitted.
(4)  In a multi storied building, if the title of the property or the registry is floor wise or
the owner produces a rent deed/lease agreement, then separate floor wise connections may
be given.
(5)  In a shop-cum-flat, one domestic supply and one non domestic supply connection
may be given.
(6)  Anyone of the following documents shall be considered as acceptable proof of
ownership or lawful occupancy of premises:
(a)  In case of Agriculture supply connection;
A copy of khasra / girdawari / jamabandi / Kisan Pass Book in the name of the applicant;
(b)  For all other connections;
(i)  Copy of sale deed / allotment letter or lease deed or rent deed in the name of the
applicant;
(ii)  Registered General Power of Attorney from the owner in favour of the applicant
alongwith (i) above;
(iii) Property tax receipt or tax demand notice as proof of ownership and rent deed or
any other legal proof of being a tenant and paying rent as proof of occupancy.

3.14 Regarding Authorization of Chartered Electrical Safety Engineer (CESE).
(Sales Instruction- U-05/2019)

   Please refer to Sales Instruction No. U-03/2016 dated 30.03.2016 vide which
instruction regarding authorization of Chartered Electrical Safety Engineer (CESE) was
issued.
In this regard, CEI, Govt. of Haryana vide office order No.98 dated 28.08.2019
(Copy enclosed as Annexure-I) has intimated that a written test was conducted by CEI,
Haryana on 07.07.2019 for authorization of Chartered Electrical Safety Engineers (CESE)
in which no candidate has qualified the written test.

321

Hence, in supersession of Sales Instruction No. U-03/2016 dated 30.03.2016
which was issued in compliance to Office order No. CEI/172 dated 18.03.2016 of the O/o
Chief Electrical Inspector to GoH, Haryana to facilitate the owner of electrical installation
for self-certification, the following has been approved to come in force with immediate effect
in compliance to the aforementioned office order No.98:-
1. The owner may get his electrical installation tested/inspected through his own
eligible engineer who fulfill the qualification and experience as per regulation 5A of the
Central Electricity Authority( Measure relating safety and Electric supply) Amendment
Regulation, 2018 notified vide notification dated 01.03.2018 followed by guidelines issued
by the Central Electricity Authority vide notification dated 21.06.2018 (Copy enclosed as
Annexure-II) till such time sufficient numbers of CESEs are authorised to self certify their
electrical installation under regulation 30 and 43 of the Central Electricity Authority(
Measure relating safety and Electric supply) Regulation, 2010, as amended from time to
time.
2. Regulation 5 (A) of CEA (Measure relating to Safety and Electric Supply) Amendment
Regulation, 2018 i.e. Qualification of Chartered Electrical Safety Engineer is reproduced as
below:
(a) The Chartered Electrical Safety Engineers shall be an Electrical Engineering degree
holder or equivalent degree with at least five years experience in operation and maintenance
of electrical installations and also should have the knowledge of the works related to
observance of electrical safety regulations or an Electrical Engineering Diploma holder with
at least 10 years of experience in operation and maintenance of electrical installations and
also should have the knowledge of the works related to observance of electrical safety
regulations.
(b) He/She shall have the knowledge of Central Electricity authority (Measures relating to
Safety and Electric Supply), Regulations, 2010 (as amended) and other relevant Act and
Regulation related to electricity supply in the respective State Government.
(c) Retired Chief Electrical Inspector/Electrical Inspector who were already notified by
Appropriate Government would be eligible for CESE. However, State Government would have
the responsibility to take the decision on exemption for test/interview for retired Chief
Electrical Inspector/Electrical Inspector.
(d) The Chartered Electrical Safety Engineers shall not hold any post in Govt./Semi
Govt./PSUs or associated with any organizations which directly or indirectly influence the
working of CESE.
(e) He/She shall for all the time in his possession have the basic testing equipments (some
basic testing equipment given in Annexure-I) as may be prescribed by the office of the Chief
Electrical Inspector/Electrical Inspector for testing of the electrical installations.
3. The authorization of existing Chartered Electrical Safety Engineers circulated vide
S.I. No. U-03/2016 is hereby cancelled with immediate effect.
The above instructions may be brought to the notice of all concerned for meticulous
compliance.

3.15 Release of connection at 33 KV level (Sales Circular No. U- 22/2018)

The existing instructions issued vide Sales Circular No. U-38/2017 dated 25.9.2017 have
been reviewed and the revised instructions are as under:-

322

(a) As per provisions of clause 4.8.3 of HERC Regulation No. 5909/HERC/T-193 dated
11.7.2016, supply to 33 KV and above rating substation would be given through
independent radial lines i.e. no tapping of 33 KV and above rating lines feeding a substation
would be allowed.
(b) It is hereby clarified that not allowing solid tapping at 33 KV level refers to not tapping
a 33 KV line between two grid substations for releasing connection to any individual/group
of consumers. This stipulation has no relevance to release of individual connections to
consumers at 33 KV level of supply on a 33 KV feeder. It is also clarified that more than
one connection can be released at 33 KV level of supply treating the same as a 33 KV
independent feeder upto 5 connections or as the case may be, an industrial feeder.
(c) As per prevailing instructions, load at 33 KV level is to be restricted to 25 MVA. This
clearly means that one or more consumers can avail load at 33 KV level upto 25 MVA
capacity.
This supersedes the sales circular No.38/2017.

3.16 Regarding Providing new domestic connections in rural areas for load
up to 2 KW. (Sales Circular No.- U- 50 /2017)

The Hon’ble CM Haryana, in order to achieve universal electrification in rural areas in line
with the SAUBHAGYA scheme, has announced that domestic connections up to 2 KW load
may be released by depositing only rupees two hundred in the first instance and the balance
connection charges may be recovered in twelve equal installments through the bi-monthly
energy bill.
2.  Accordingly, in order to implement the aforesaid directions of Hon’ble CM
Haryana, it has been decided that henceforth new domestic connections up to 2 KW load
in rural areas will be released on payment of only rupees two hundred in the first instance,
with balance connection charges to be paid in twelve equal installments along with the bi-
monthly energy bill. For the sake of clarity, ‘rural areas’ mean all areas falling under Gram
Panchayats.
3.  Special camps in association with the Gram Panchayat may be organized in
villages under your jurisdiction for providing on the spot domestic connection to release
maximum number of domestic connections as per ibid instructions.

3.19   Reduction of load – Change of CTs (Sales Instruction No. U-
09/2017)

While reviewing the pendency of release of connections/ extension of load/ reduction of
load, it has been observed that there is considerable delay in effecting the ROL cases due
to insistence for reducing CTs matching with the reduced load.
2. The technical aspect have been gone through and it has been observed that the 33
KV and 11 KV CTs are tested in five levels/ stages i.e. 1%, 5%, 20%, 100% & 120% and LT
CTs are tested in four levels/ stages i.e. 5%, 20%, 100% & 120%.
3. The matter has been reconsidered and it has been decided that so long as there is no
change of voltage level in case of reduction of load, there is no need to replace the existing
CTs.

3.20 Taking of loading position – Release of connection. (Sales Instruction
No. U- 04/2016)

Different procedures are being followed in the field for considering the loading position of
power T/F in case of release of industrial and other category connection above 11 KV level.
Now, the matter discussed in the meeting of UHBVN, DHBVN and HVPNL held on dated
26.02.2016 and decided as under.
Presently, 11 KV industrial connections from 33 KV and above Sub-Stations in DISCOMs
are being released as per the Max. Demand recorded on the Power T/F, Feeders and
Distribution T/F etc. whereas, for the purpose of creation/augmentation of new Sub-
Stations, installed capacity of the feeding end Power T/F is being considered1.2 times its
rated capacity for augmentation or creation of new Nigam Sub-Station and 1.0 times the
rated capacity in case of industrial and other category load.
Now, it has been decided that to release 33 KV and above load, feasibility of release of that
load should be considered only if the total capacity of that feeding end power T/F comes
within the limit i.e. 1.2 times the rated capacity of that power T/F and max. demand
recorded of that power T/F. This is to avoid any overloading and un-necessary harassment

324

to the consumer .

3.24 Procedure for release of connection under Industrial Policy, 2015 (Sales
Circular No. U- 42/2016)

Please refer to S.C. No. U-21/2016 dated 27.06.2016 issued in compliance to
Enterprise Promotion Policy (EPP)-2015 and Industry Department notification No.
49/53/2005-41B1 dated 03.06.2016 vide which the concurrent powers were delegated.
  The detailed procedure regarding release of connections applied through Single
Window Portal on www.investharyana.nic.in is as under:-
  For success of the Industrial Policy, 2015, Single Roof System has been
installed in the Haryana Enterprises Promotion Board (HEPB). The investor shall apply on
the Single Window Portal www.investharyana.nic.in for all types of approval on Common
Application Form (CAF) relating to all the Departments. All the projects with investment
more than 10 Cr. and involving CLU cases of more than one acre shall be dealt by the
Executive Empowered Committee (EEC) having CE/Comml. as the Nodal Officer who will
sanction all the cases upto 5000 KVA/KW (irrespective of load) and will get all the cases
above 5000 KVA/KW sanctioned from the Competent Authority. Similarly, concerned SE
‘OP’ is the Nodal Officer for District Level Clearance Committee (DLCC) involving all the
projects with investment less then Rs. 10 Cr. and CLU cases of less than one acre and will
sanction all the cases upto 2000 KVA/KW (irrespective of load) and will get all the cases

326

above 2000 KVA/KW sanctioned from the Competent Authority.
  The investor have to fill up the CAF and sent it to the Desk Officer (HEPB).
Who will forward it to all the Departments for necessary approvals within the time bound
manner. The Nodal Officer will forward the complete CAF to the respective SE’s ‘OP’ for
submitting the technical feasibility regarding release of the temporary / permanent
connection load and charges (processing charges, ACD, Service Connection Charges,
Deposit Estimate etc. etc.) to be deposited by the investor to the Nodal Officer within four
days positively otherwise entire responsibility shall lie on concerned office. Also, will get the
estimate prepared and sanctioned (Circle/Divn. wise login details are Annexed as Annexure
–I).
  The SDO ‘OP’ will download the required papers from the SE/XEN Login ID
and prepare a consumer case file. Further, the investor shall deposit the requisite charges
with the HEPB who will transfer the amount to the UHBVN account no. 00384010000170,
IFSC Code ORBC0100038 of Oriental Bank of Commerce Sec-17B, Chandigarh. On receipt
of the payment, O/o of the FA/Hq. will intimate to the Nodal Officer and concerned SE ‘OP’
regarding receipt of the amount. SE ‘OP’ shall get the demand notice issued within Two day
alongwith the difference of the charges to be deposited by the investor if any and send to
the Nodal Officer. After receipt of the requisite charges and test report from the investor,
the test report shall be verified and intimated to the Nodal Officer who will sanction the
load/got it sanctioned from the competent authority and intimate to the concerned SE ‘OP’
who will get the connection released from the SDO ‘OP’ concerned as per the time line
prescribed in the Right to Service Act.

3.30 Service Connection Charges from the industrialists seeking electric
connection in the area developed by HSIIDC (S.I. No. U-31/2010)
A few Industries Associations have been representing that Service Connection Charges may
not be levied to the consumers whose industries are located in the HSIIDC Industrial
Estates. In support of their contention, they have been stating that since all the electrical
infrastructure has been laid by HSIIDC and the entire cost for the infrastructure has been
recovered from the allottees, any further payment of Service Connection Charges by the
Distribution Utilities will amount to double charging for the same infrastructure.
  So the matter has been reviewed and decided that if the entire electrical
infrastructure for HSIIDC Industrial Estates has been laid by the Corporation, the Service
Connection Charges in the Industrial Estates may not be charged.
  Further, any extension in sub-mains will be done by the applicant himself for
the loads 20 to 50 KW and beyond 50 KW the connection is necessarily to be released as
HT connection for which all equipment etc. will be supplied by the consumers.

3.31 Sanction of loads – Demand factor/Diversity Factor (Sales Instructions
No. U- 25/2010)

It has been observed that field officers while assessing the impact of new incoming load on
the system are dividing the max. load of the applicant (Contract Demand or connected load)
for HT consumers with a uniform diversity factor of 2.0 (except in case of steel
furnaces/steel rolling mills) in terms of sales circular no. 26/97 dated 16.07.97.

329

The matter has been reviewed and it has been observed the diversity factor is the ratio of
sum of individual maximum demands of consumers and max. demand of the system.
 Diversity Factor = Sum of individual maximum demand of consumers
    Max. demand on power system
The calculations of impact of load of new incoming applicant on the system by taking into
account diversity factor is wrong as diversity factor reflects diversity in max. demand of
various consumers at different points of times. Whereas for the purpose of impact of
individual consumer demand factor is to be taken into consideration which is the ratio of
max. demand of individual consumer to the contract demand/connected load.
  Demand Factor = Maximum demand of individual consumer
    Contract demand or connected load
The values of demand factor have been given in the sales manual for all categories of
industries and consumers. A copy of the same is attached for ready reference.
It has therefore been decided that henceforth impact of load reflected on the system will be
calculated by multiplying the demand factor with C.D or C.L.
  Impact of load = C.D or C.L X Demand Factor
For the purpose of estimating energy consumption of individual consumer connected load
factor has to be taken into account.
  Connected load factor = Demand Factor x Load Factor
  Load factor = Average Power
    Max. Power Demand
For example an automobile industry having contract demand of 75KVA the energy
consumption will be.
. Unit consumed in the year= 75 KVA x Power Factor x 0.65 x 0.25x 8760
        = 106762.5 Units  (8760 being number of hours in year)
It has been further observed that field officers are not taking correctly current carrying
capacity of conductor. Different officers are assuming different values. Henceforth following
values of current carrying capacity will be taken
Sr. No.  Conductor  Equivalent
Aluminum Area

 These instruction will supersede all earlier instruction issued on the subject.

refunded or not.
3.  It is also clarified that such applications upon revival be dealt as per Sales
Circular No. U-24/2021 and up-to-date amendments which broadly means applications
upto 50BHP in Non-notified areas and upto 35 BHP in Notified areas can be considered for
revival. Notably, there is no requirement to insist on solar-powered connections up to 10
BHP, as this condition was made obligatory for tubewell applications received from January
01, 2019, to December 31, 2021.
4.  All concerned for strict and meticulous compliance with immediate effect.

4.7  No requirement of 'No Objection Certificate' (NOC) from the co-sharers
regarding instructions issued vide memo No. Ch-90/TR-90/DPR/CE/C-I dated
10.10.2024

  In the subject cited matter, it is stated that vide letter bearing office memo no.
Ch-84/TR-90/DPR/CE/C-I dated 05.06.2024 relating to release of tubewell connection it
was circulated that connection may be released without insisting for submission of prior

336

‘No Objection Certificate' from the co-sharers on furnishing the indemnity bond and
undertaking. The above was in compliance of judgement passed by Hon'ble Punjab and
Haryana High Court in CWP No. 26395 of 2017 titled as Jahid Hassan Vs State of Haryana
& Ors.
2.   It is hereby clarified that the benefit of instruction dated 05.06.2024, is also
extended to tubewell connection holder when shifting of connection or change of name in
favour of his/her legal heirs is sought. This is, however, subject to fulfilment of other
requirement as specified in The Electricity Act 2003. Therefore, in all such cases also, an
indemnity bond & undertaking in the enclosed format be taken from the applicant.
3.  All concerned are requested to comply with the directions meticulously.
…………………………………………………………………………………………………………………..

4.8   Issue of Not Obtaining No Objection Certificate (NOC) from the Co-Sharers
regarding instructions issued vide memo No.Ch-84/TR-90/DPR/CE/C-I dated:
05.06.2024

  The Hon’ble Punjab and Haryana High Court, Chandigarh in CWP No. 26395
of 2017 titled as Jahid Hassan V/s State of Haryana & Ors has ordered to release the
electricity connection to the petitioner without insisting for submission of prior ‘No
Objection Certificate’ from the co-sharers, subject to the petitioner fulfilling the other
requirements of the Electricity Act and on furnishing an indemnity bond to secure the
interests of the respondent-Distribution Licensee and that no harm would be done to the
property of the respondent-Distribution Licensee in releasing the tubewell connection and,
an undertaking that in case any damage is caused, the petitioner will compensate the
Distribution Companies and hold the Distribution Companies harmless against any claim.
2.  The operative part of judgment dated 21.03.2023 is reproduced as under:-
"In view of the aforesaid judicial pronouncement of this Court, the present writ petition is
disposed of with a direction to the respondents that subject to the petitioner fulfilling the other
requirements of the Electricity Act and on his furnishing an indemnity bond to secure the
interests of the respondent-Distribution Licensee and that no harm would be done to the
property of the respondent-Distribution Licensee in releasing the tubewell connection and an
undertaking that in case any damage is caused, the petitioner will compensate the
Electricity Board and hold the electricity Board harmless against any claim, shall consider to
release the electricity connection to the petitioner without insisting for submission of prior ‘No
Objection Certificate’ from the co-sharers. The electricity connection shall be released to the
petitioner within a period of 30 days submission of the necessary documents and on fulfilling
of the requisite statutory requirements.”

3.  Indemnity Bond and Affidavit that would be obtained from the applicant, as
highlighted in the above judgement, are enclosed herewith as Annexure-I and II
respectively.

4.  The copy of Order of Hon’ble Punjab and Haryana High Court in the matter is
also enclosed herewith for strict and meticulous compliance by all concerned, please.

4.11 Release of new tubewell connections with 3 Star (earlier 5 Star) energy
efficient motor-pumpsets. (Sales Circular No. 06/2023).

 Hon’ble CM, Haryana during the Budget Speech for FY 2023-24 has announced to
provide the tubewell connections applied from 1st January, 2019 to 31st December, 2021.
Accordingly, it has been decided to issue Demand Notices to the applicant who have applied
for tubewell connection from 01.01.2019 to 31.12.2021 subject to the following guidelines
which are detailed as under: -
A. Eligibility
The tubewell connections upto 10 BHP shall be released by HAREDA on solar off grid mode
and the tubewell applicants/farmers above 10 BHP to 35 BHP shall be eligible to release
new tubewell connections by the Nigam.
B. Issue of Demand Notices
The demand notices shall be issued within 15 days by all the SDOs (OP) from the date of
issuance of Sales Circular i.e. on 25.05.2023 to all the eligible applicants through registered
post for deposition of Rs.30,000/- as consent money within a period of three months from
the date of issue of demand notice that shall be adjusted later on in the cost of
infrastructure.
C. 3 Star Rated (5 star before 01.02.2020) Energy Efficient Motor Pumpsets
1. All such pending tubewell connections shall be allowed to be released with 3 Star
rating (5 star before 01.02.2020) submersible motor pumpsets.
2. The motor-pumpsets shall be strictly in accordance to the approved specification of
the Nigam with 5 years warranty. However, the warranty clause shall be executed between
the dealer/firm and the applicant/farmer directly.
3. Before dispatch of the motor-pumpsets to the authorized dealers, the manufacturing
firm shall offer the material for factory inspection in lot of 100 Nos. (min.) which shall be
duly inspected by the authorized inspection team of the Nigam so as to ensure quality.
4. The applicant/farmer shall deposit the copy of bill and warranty card in the
concerned Sub-Divisional offices which shall be duly cross verified from the manufacturing

341

firm by the SDOs (OP) concerned by making communication to their email ids. Tubewell
connection can only be released after authentication of the required energy standard viz 3
star rating (earlier 5 Star) from the said authentication of the required energy standard viz
3 star rating (earlier 5 Star) from the said manufacturing firm and verification that supplied
motor-pumpsets and verification that supplied motor-pumpset stands inspected by the
Nigam from the dispatch instructions issued by the MM wing that can be obtained from the
manufacturing firm or from the MM wing of the Nigam.
5. The process of purchase of motor from empaneled firm/rates etc. shall be intimated
in due course of time.

D. Cost of Electrical Infrastructure
1. All AP supply connections shall be released as per HERC Regulation No.
HERC/34/2016 dated 11.07.16 on Duty to Supply Electricity on request, Power to recover
expenditure in providing supply and power to require security Regulation, 2016 and 1st
amendment, 2020 circulated vide Sales Circular No. U-09/2020 and the expenditure shall
be recovered as under: -
“Actual expenditure to be incurred for release of connection which shall include
cost of LT/HT line and that of distribution transformer. In case more than one
consumers are released connections from the same transformer, the cost of
distribution transformer shall be shared on prorata basis corresponding to the
load of each consumer.”
2. It shall be ensured by the XENs (OP) that estimates of electrical infrastructure of all
the eligible applicants stands prepared by the sub-divisions under their control. The
applicants shall be allowed to deposit the infrastructure cost as per the aforementioned
provision of HERC Supply Code Regulations.

E. Micro Irrigation/Under Ground Pipeline System
On account of excessive exploitation of ground water and huge burden of RE subsidy, the
condition of installation of Micro Irrigation/Under Ground Pipeline System shall mandatory
as under:-
i.In villages where water table is available upto 100 ft. from ground surface, applicant/farmer
shall have option of installation of Under Ground Pipeline System or Micro Irrigation
Systems for release of new tubewell connections. In case of UGPL, Self certification from
applicant for installation of UGPL system shall suffice that shall be cross verified by the
Area incharge before release of tubewell connections.
ii.In villages where water table is below 100 ft. from ground surface, installation of Micro
Irrigation Systems shall be the pre-requisite condition for release of new tubewell
connections,. For this purpose, farmer/applicant can install any type of Micro Irrigation
System for example Sprinkler irrigation system, Drip irrigation system and/or Mini
Sprinkler irrigation system.
It may be the case that applicant has already having MI system installed in his/her fields.
For authentication of installation of MI system, a certificate from the department of MICADA
shall be mandatory. However, for convenience of the farmers/applicants in obtaining
certificate from the department of MICADA, the Sub-divisional officer shall co-ordinate with
MICADA for obtaining the certificate. SDO (OP) shall obtain additional details from the
farmer/applicant about his/her fields where new tubewell connection is proposed and MI
system is mandatory by writing to him/her immediately as per Annexure-A. Thereafter, all
such details shall be punched by the SDO(OP) office on an exclusive web-page that shall

342

be made available on Nigam’s portal. This web-page shall be integrated with the department
of MICADA, where they shall issue online certificates after verification.
State Govt. is also providing subsidy through the department of MICADA for installation of
Micro Irrigation systems. Therefore, where MI system is yet to be installed by the
farmer/applicant, both erection of infrastructure and process for release of MI subsidy
through MICADA will be taken up simultaneously in order to keep the average time for
release of connection to bare minimum.
iii.The list containing village-wise Ground Water Level as notified by Irrigation & Water
Resources Department, Haryana vide Notification No.2/5/2022-1IW dated 22.04.2022 is
enclosed herewith as Annexure-B.
F. Seniority
1. In order to expedite the release of pending tubewell connections, village wise
connections shall be released in one go as it would aid in faster erection of electrical
infrastructure from village to village. Accordingly, all SDO Op will ensure that village wise
seniority is maintained in the Sub Divn.
2. The village wise seniority for release of tubewell connections, will be further sub-
divided as per following classifications: :-
a) In case where spare capacity is available on the existing transformer and only cable
upto 20mtr is required.
b) In case where spare capacity is available on the existing transformer and only LT
line is required.
c) In case where spare capacity is not available on the existing transformer and
augmentation of the T/F is required with a cable upto 20 mtr.
d)  Augmentation of existing T/F & erection of LT Line.
e)  Providing additional T/F with erection of HT/LT line.
G. Other Guidelines
1. SDOs (OP) shall also issue the notices to all the applicants upto 10 BHP intimating
that their tubewell application has become dormant for the Nigam and the same has been
forwarded to HAREDA for releasing tubewell connection on Solar Off Grid Mode.
2. SEs (OP) at district level will convene meeting with HAREDA authorities & will share
the information of applicants upto 10 BHP with them.
3. MICADA & Nigam’s officers shall convene a joint meeting in villages where water level
is below 100 ft. and educate the applicants regarding process for installing MI system,
subsidy admissible and process of obtaining certificate regarding installation of Micro-
Irrigation system
4. Metering will be done through Non-smart electronic meter and cost of the meter shall
be charged from the farmers/applicants. Cable from transformer to meter shall be provided
by the Nigam whereas farmer will be responsible for providing the cable from meter to
motor.”
5. Control Panel/Starter and LT capacitors will be provided by the farmers at his own
cost.
6. Maximum length of LT line emanating from the transformer for release of tubewell
connection shall be 300 meters (upto 5 poles) i.e. no LT line shall exceed 300 meters.
7. Distribution Transformer up to 100 KVA capacity only shall be allowed with
maximum loading of 80% of its capacity. Existing Transformer can also be augmented as

343

per requirement while releasing the connection.
8. The span of HT/LT line is to be taken as 70 meters. The ACSR conductor to be used
shall be of size 50 mm2.
9. Connection will be released from nearest LT/HT/Transformer irrespective of
jurisdiction of sub-division and application shall be transferred to the sub-division under
jurisdiction of which the transformer falls after release of connection.
10. It shall also be ensured by the SDO ‘OP’ concerned that the new tubewell applicant
is not in default of any kind of dues with the Nigam.
11. All new tubewell connections shall be metered and shall be released on AP feeder
only.
12. In case of demise of original AP applicants before release of connection, the
connection can be released to his legal heir.
H. Payment of interest
  It has been decided to pay interest on the amount deposited by new tubewell
applicants against Consent Money, and amount towards electrical infrastructure if the
connections are not released within six months as under:-
i. Interest shall be given at the rate applicable on ACD on the cost deposited by the new
tubewell applicants against Consent Money, and amount towards electrical infrastructure.
ii.The interest shall become due as detailed below :-
(a) Consent money   -  From the date of deposition.
(b) Cost for infrastructure * -   After six months from the date of
(Estimated cost minus Consent money) deposition of infrastructure cost.
* If connection is not released within six months (from the date of deposition of infrastructure
cost) due to reasons not attributable to the farmers/applicants.
  The above instructions should be brought to the notice of all concerned for
careful and meticulous compliance and wide publicity shall also be ensured through local
Cable TV network, newspapers, distribution of pamphlets & SMS.

4.13 Release of tubewell connection – Clarification for Villages with Ground
Water Table below 40 Meters. (Sales Circular No. U- 21/2023).

  In compliance to Sales Circular No. U-06/2023 vide which instructions were
issued to serve demand notices to the new applicants who had applied during the period
01.01.2019 to 31.12.2021 with applied load beyond 10 BHP to 35 BHP. It was also decided
that the connection upto 10 BHP will be released by the Department of NRE & HAREDA on
standalone solar mode.
2.  This issue has been re-considered and it has been decided that new tubewell
applicants (whom prospective connections are to be released is in villages where ground
water has gone beyond 40 meters) will have the option to apply for extension of applied
motor load. If they opt for extension of applied motor-load for more than 10 BHP; their
application shall be considered for Grid connection by the Nigam.
3.  SDO ‘OP’ shall intimate this facility to the concerned applicants by issuing a
notice of 15 days within 2 days of issue of Sales Circular. A window of 15 days on the lapse
of validity of the above notice shall be provided in the online portal for interested applicants
to apply for extension of load.
4.  For the applicants who become eligible for the Grid connections after their
applications of extension of load, the issuance of Demand notices and other condition as
laid down in Sales Circular No. U-06/2023 shall be followed strictly. Their seniority shall
not be altered and shall be considered from the date of their original application for new
connection.
5.  CE/IT shall make the necessary changes in Online portal to accommodate the
above facility. It is also clarified that under these instructions, since the application of
extension of Load will be received before release of connection, therefore, Service
Connection Charges @ 1500/- per BHP (as provided in Sales Circular No. U-48/2017) will
not be applicable for such applications of EoL.
6.  All other terms & conditions of Sales Circular No. U-06/2023 for release of
tubewell connections shall remain applicable. List of village wise Ground Water Level as
notified by Irrigation and Water Resources Department, Haryana vide Notification No.
2/5/2022-1IW dated 22.04.2022 is enclosed.

shall also be given equal opportunity by reviving them by the SE(OP) concerned. The activity
of reviving tubewell applications shall be completed by 15.09.2021.
3.  Thereafter, on 16.09.2021 demand notices, in one go, shall be issued to all the
eligible applicants seeking new tubewell connections in the notified area as detailed above
through registered post for deposition of Rs. 30,000/- as consent money that shall be
adjusted later on in the cost of infrastructure.
4.  The new tubewell connections in the notified areas shall be released subject to
the following mandatory conditions:
i.The farmer will adopt micro irrigation mandatorily if depth of tubewell exceeds 100ft.
ii.No connection greater than 35 BHP shall be released.
5.  Extension of load, RCO and shifting of connection shall also be permitted
subject to same stipulation as mentioned at Sr. No. (i) & (ii).
6.  All the aforementioned eligible new tubewell connections in the notified area
shall be released in the second phase of release of tubewell connections as per the detailed
guidelines mentioned in Sales Circular No. UTW-24/2021 dated 26.07.2021 except the
installation of MI system and maximum capacity of tubewell connection shall be dealt as
per Para 4 above.
7.   It might be the case that the applicants may now be requiring higher capacity
of motor-pumpset then that was initially applied for. Here, it is clarified that such requests
for EoL/RoL shall be considered by the sub-divisions. The instructions/process for dealing
such requests already stand issued by the Nigam which are annexed herewith for ready
reference as Annexure-I & II.
8.  It is also clarified that there is no bar for receiving fresh Tubewell applications
in the notified areas.
   This also supersedes Sales circular No. U-23/2021.

4.16 Not releasing Grid Connected Tubewell connections if an Off Grid Solar
Powered Tubewell connections exist (Sales Circular No. U- 27/2021)

As you may all are aware that Department of NRE & HAREDA, Haryana has also been
releasing Off Grid Solar Powered New Tubewell Connections in the State at highly
subsidized rates. And, UHBVN has also undertaken to release new tubewell connections
applied upto 31.12.2018.
2.  As, there is no sharing of information at the time of application between both
said departments, therefore, there might be a possibility that the farmers may avail the
benefit of subsidized solar connection from Department of NRE & HAREDA and also seek
new grid connected tubewell connection from the Nigam.
3.  It is, therefore, clarified that Grid connected new tubewell connection cannot
be released on the same site if the applicant has installed an Off Grid Solar tubewell
Connection.
Further, in case, some applicants have obtained both types of tubewell connections (i.e.,
Grid Connected as well as Solar Powered Off Grid) at the same site, a notice shall
immediately be served to disconnect their Grid Connected tubewell connections and action
be taken against the existing ones latest by 31.08.2021.

4.17 Shifting of tubewell connection from one site to another in the event
of acquisition of land by HUDA or other state agencies (S.C. No. U-32/2021).

Please refer to the sales circular No. U-39/2010 dated 19.11.2010 vide which it was decided
to allow shifting of tubewell connection from one site to another in the event of acquisition
of land by HUDA or other State agencies. Now, the matter has been re-considered and
decided that shifting of tubewell connection would be allowed subject to the fulfillment of
following conditions.
1. Proof indicating acquisition of land by HUDA or other State agencies.
2. Availability of nearby power supply infrastructure as agriculture feeder at the
changed/new location.
3. The expenditure incurred on account of dismantlement at the existing premises and
on account of erection at new site will be borne by the consumer.
4. New A&A form is to be submitted.
5. Certificate to the effect that all pending dues are cleared irrespective of the fact that
connection is connected or disconnected.
6. Shifting of tubewell connection from one site to another is permitted on the
production of certificate of legal heir from competent authority/court in case of death of
original applicant with an affidavit by the new applicant owning the responsibility against
any legal complications at later stage.
7. The consumer would be entitled to alternate tubewell connection(s) in this category
either in his un-acquired land or over the agricultural land that he may purchase elsewhere
in the State upto two years from the date of PDCO of the existing tubewell connection.
8. Alternate connection would be provided within a period of three months of the
application of the land owner.

347

  Sales Circular No. U-39/2010 dated 19.11.2010 is hereby superseded.
  The above instructions should be brought to notice of all concerned for
meticulous compliance.

4.19 Star ratings of motor pumpset for extension of load - Clarification
thereof. (Sales Circular No. U-16/2020)

As you are aware that new tubewell connections are being released with 5 Star rated energy
efficient motor pumpsets. Earlier, to these instructions, farmers/applicants were required
to install 4 Star rated motor pumpsets for release of tubewell connections as provided in
Sales Circular No. U-41/2009.
2.  Both the consumers (i) who have been given connection with 5 Star motor
pumpset and (ii) who have been given connections prior to the provision of 5 Star motor
pumpset may be approaching field offices for extension of load. In this context some
references have been received seeking clarification about what Star Rating of motor-
pumpset, Nigam should insist for extension of load.
3.  This issue for extension of load is clarified as under:-

a)  For tubewell consumers released with 5 Star motor pumpset:
 For such cases, necessary provision for extension of load is already covered in
Clause-15 of Sales Circular No. U-27/2019. The contents of the relevant clause are
reproduced as under: -
“In case any applicant seeks extension of load before release of connection, he/she shall be
provided higher capacity motor (as per extended load) on subsidized rates. In case,

349

farmer/consumer opts for extension of load after release of connection, he/she will pay the
purchase rate of the Nigam.”
 The applicant be allowed to deposit the requisite amount (as detailed in Sales
Circular No. U-27/2019) in the sub-division alongwith consent to provide motor pumpset
with legend 5 Star rating (now 3 star). The details of such consumers will subsequently, be
intimated to the O/o CE/MM, UHBVN, Panchkula by the Sub-division for arranging the
motor pumpset.

b) For tubewell consumers who have been released connections before the
provision of 5 Star motor pumpsets:-
 Such tubewell consumers (requiring submersible motor pumpsets) be allowed to
procure same with star rating equal or more than 3 Star (earlier 5 star) from open market.
 However, applicant requiring monoblock pumpsets be allowed to procure same from
Open market with star rating equal or above 2 Star (earlier 4 Star) in sync with this office
clarification given vide CP-35/TR-95(90)/TW/2019/CE/C-I dated 09.07.2020 (Copy
enclosed).
 These consumers shall be required to submit copy of original bill in support of
procurement of the motor pumpset with aforementioned rating in the O/o concerned SDO
‘OP’. XEN ‘OP’/ SDO ‘OP’ shall further ensure the genuineness of the bill and star rating of
the motor pumpset procured by the consumer before effecting the extension of load.

4.20 Clarification regarding adjustment of cost of existing Transformer in the
estimate for release of new tubewell connection.(S.C. No. U-37/2019)

 Please refer to Annexure-I of Sales Circular No. U-35/2016 dated 29.08.2016 vide
which it has been notified that the applicant shall deposit the following cost of electrical
infrastructure i.e. estimated cost for release of tubewell connection as per HERC Regulation
No. HERC/34/2016 dated 11.07.16 on Duty to Supply Electricity on request, Power to
recover expenditure in providing supply and power to require Security Regulation, 2016.
  “Actual expenditure to be incurred for release of connection which shall include
cost of LT/HT line and that of distribution transformer. In case more than one consumers are
released connections from the same transformer, the cost of distribution transformer shall be
shared on prorate basis corresponding to the load of each consumer"
 Keeping in view the representations received from the field regarding adjustment of
the cost of existing 25/63 KVA T/F in case of augmentation with new 63/100 KVA T/F at
the time of release of connection or not.
 The matter has been considered by the management and decided as under: -
 The cost of augmentation of transformer to be borne by the prospective AP consumer
shall be the per BHP cost derived as below: -
 KVA x 0.8 (PF) x 0.8 (Loading factor) / 0.746.
 63 x 0.8 x 0.8 / 0.746 = 54 BHP
 However, cost of all other material will remain same as per previous trend shall be
borne by the prospective AP consumer only.

350

 As the existing tubewell consumer (irrespective of his load i.e. 10 BHP, 15 BHP, 20
BHP) on 10/16/25 KVA transformer has already paid the relevant charges for release of
tubewell connection prevailing at that time and the 10/16/25 KVA transformer has to be
augmented to 63 KVA transformer to release another 20 BHP new tubewell connection.
 Suppose, the estimated cost of augmentation of 25 KVA transformer with 63 KVA
(taking 0 value of the 25 KVA transformer) is Rs.60,000/-.
 As the existing consumer has already paid the charges so the proportionate cost for
20 BHP new connection comes to be = 60,000 divided by 54 i.e the maximum capacity of
load that can be released on 63 KVA Transformer and multiplied by 20 = Rs. 22222.22 say
Rs.22223/- (60000x20/54).
 Similarly, suppose, there are 2 No. existing tubewell connections having on existing
63 KVA transformer and the transformer is to be augmented to 100 KVA to release another
25 BHP new connection.
 Suppose, the estimated cost of augmentation of 63 KVA transformer with 100 KVA
(taking 0 value of the 63 KVA transformer) is Rs.10,0000/-.
 As the existing consumers have already paid the charges so the proportionate cost
for 25 BHP new connection comes to be = 100000 divided by 86 i.e. the maximum capacity
for released load on 100 KVA Transformer (100000x25/86).Rs. 29069.76 say Rs.29070/-.
 The dismantled transformer shall not be handed over to the consumer in case the
same is installed even under Self-Execution scheme.
For accounting purpose, the estimate of new consumer will remain special instead of
deposit estimate as difference of cost (i.e. actual cost minus share cost deposited by the
consumer) shall be borne by the Nigam. The procedure for accounting of expenditure is as
under:
1. The assets of new transformer will be made with full cost of new augmented
transformer.
2. The share cost of transformer deposited by consumer shall be considered as
consumer contribution in GH-47.
3. The remaining value (Total cost - cost deposited by consumer) shall be borne by the
Nigam till the balance load is utilized either in release of new connection or extension of
load by the existing consumers on the said augmented transformer.
 The above clarification may be brought to the notice of all concerned for strict and
meticulous compliance.

4.25 Shifting of Tubewell connections. (S.C. No. U-33/2001)

Please refer to sales Circular No. 04/2000 issued by this office Memo No. Ch-173/
TR/95/90/Losse-2, dated 07.02.2000 wide which instruction were issued that shifting of
Tubewell connection on account of failure of Bore or for any other reason can be permitted
in the boundary of the same villages land area and in the name of same of consumers.
The matter has further been reviewed and it has been decided that shifting of the tubewell
connections on account of salinity of water, failure of bore or for any other reason can be
allowed anywhere in the jurisdiction of UHBVN subject to the following conditions: -
(i) The ground water cell of Irrigation Department shall certify the salinity/non-
suitability of water in respect of the tubewell to be shifted in case the same has been sought
on the grounds of salinity of water. The suitability of water in respect of new site where this
tubewell is required to be shifted would also be certified by the Ground Water Cell.
(ii) Shifting would also be allowed in case of failure of bore of the tubewell or any other
reason to which the shifting has been requested.
(iii) The shifting would be permitted in case of both the connected as well as disconnected
tubewells, subject to the conditions mentioned in para-I & II above.
(iv) The land which may be situated anywhere in the UHBVN jurisdiction, should be in
the same name in which the original tubewell is situated. The shifting of tubewell will be
allowed without any change in name.
(v) The applicant for shifting of tubewell would bear the entire cost of shifting i.e. the
dismantlement of old line and erection of new line and the cost of additional material, if
required, at new location.
(vi) The consumer shall not be a defaulter on account of payment of any electricity bill.
The above instructions may be brought to the notice of all concern for careful and
meticulous compliance

SECTION - 5  INSTALLATION OF SOLAR ROOFTOP

5.1 Standard Operating Procedure for State Financial Assistance in Roof
Top Solar. (Sales Circular No. USolar-18/2024)

Following Standard Operating Procedure (SoP) shall be adopted for State Financial
Assistance for Rooftop Solar (RTS) installations: -
Eligibility criteria
The eligibility criterion for the consumers to avail the State Financial Assistance (SFA) in
addition to the Central Financial Assistance (CFA) for installation of Roof Top Solar upto a
load of 2 kW shall be as follows:-
1.  The applicant should have a Domestic supply (DS) connection with sanctioned (S.L.)
upto or equal to 2 kW.
2.  The annual income of the consumer should be upto Rs. 1.80 Inca for Category 1
consumers and from 1.8 lacs to Rs. 3 Lacs for Category II consumers as per Parivar Pehchan
Patra (PPP) database.
3.  The average consumption of the consumer shall be upto 200 units/month during
preceding Financial Year or upto 2400 units annually in the preceding Financial Year.
4.  The scheme shall be applicable for the 50,000 consumers on the first come first serve
basis'
Technical specifications
The technical specifications of the Rooftop solar plant shall be same as that of PM Surya
Ghar: Muft Bijli Yojana as amended from time to time. The same could be fetched from the
https://www.pmsuryaghar.gov.in/link.
Subsidy Structure
The subsidy structure for the Central Financial Assistance (CFA) and the State Financial
Assistance (SFA) shall be as follows:-
(i)  Rs 30,000/kW or 60% of Benchmark Cost per kW upto 2 kW (whichever is lower)
shall be provided by MNRE as Central Financial Assistance (CFA).
(ii) For Category I consumer with Annual income upto Rs 1.8 Lacs:
Rs. 25,000/kW or 40% of the billed amount per kW upto 2 kW (whichever is lower) shall be
provided by the DISCOMs (on behalf of State Govt.) as State Financial Assistance. For
Category II consumer with Annual income from Rs 1.8 Lacs to 3 Lacs:
Rs. 10000/KW or 20% of the billed amount per Kw upto 2 Kw (whichever is lower) shall be
provided by the DISCOMs (on behalf of State Govt.) as State Financial Assistance.
(iii)  In case the actual project Cost/billed amount is lower than the tentative Central
Financial Assistance and the State Financial Assistance combined, the State Financial
Assistance will be limited upto the difference of the actual Project Cost/billed Amount and
the Central Financial Assistance.
(iv)  For the purpose of the calculation of Financial Assistance (Central and State) the
methodology as provided by MNRE in the guidelines amended from time to time shall be
adopted.

354

Online Portal
The consumer will have to apply on the UHBVN Solar portal at the URL:
https://sfa.uhbvn.org.in/#no-back-button for claiming the State Financial Assistance
(SFA) and on the PM Surya Ghar Portal at link:
https://www.pmsuryaghar.gov.in/consumerLogin for claiming the Central Financial
Assistance (CFA).
Following steps shall be followed on the UHBVN Solar portal while making a valid
application: -
a) The consumer will have to apply on the UHBVN Solar portal wherein he will have to
enter the PPP ID and the same will be validated through an OTP on the registered mobile
number.
b)  The list of members mapped to the PPP Id will be available. The consumer will select
the name of the applicant and the electricity Account linked to the member selected will
then be displayed. In case the Electricity account no. is not mapped then the consumer will
have to get the same mapped as per the procedure of Haryana Parivar Pehchan Authority
(HPPA).
c)  The eligibility of the consumer after entering the PPP ID and the Electricity Account
No. shall then be verified.
d)  Once the eligibility criteria is met, the applicant will be prompted to enter the
consumption of the preceding FY on Monthly/Bi-Monthly basis.
e) The yearly consumption filled by the applicant will then be duly verified by the Billing
Software/SDO (OP). The genuineness of the application shall be verified by the concerned
sub-division and processed within 5 days. The application processing fee of Rs. 1000/-
shall be waived off for the applicants eligible for State Financial Assistance (SFA) and shall
be reimbursed by the State Government to the DISCOM.
f)  After all the above criteria are met, the consumer will then be eligible for the State
Financial Assistance. The applicant shall then enter the application reference code of the
National Portal.
g)  If availing the loan facility, the applicant shall provide the Account No./Loan Account
No. and the IFSC Code of the nominated bank from which loan is being availed for the
purpose.
h)  It shall be responsibility of the concerned SDO (OP) to verify the latitude and
longitudes before releasing the connection of the applicant.
i)  The consumer will then be guided through the already existing procedure upto
release of connection.
j)  After the release of connection, the consumer will have to upload the following
documents for the initiation of the process of the State Financial Assistance (SFA) on the
portal:-
1. GST bill received from the vendor to the consumer for the supply, installation and
commissioning of the Rooftop Solar (RTS) plant.
2. Cancelled cheque of self-account/ Loan account in which the consumer wants to avail
the State Financial Assistance (SFA).
k)  The application will then be forwarded from the Sub-division to Division for the
calculation of the State Financial Assistance and the same will be sanctioned by the
concerned Divisions in the Self-account/Loan-account (as the case may be) by drawing
limits against the scheme from the FA/HQ, Panchkula.

355

l)  Preference will be given to the vendors who will not take any payment from Category
I beneficiaries and will receive their payment after installation through central and state
financial assistance. Payment shall be released within 7 days of the installation inspection
failing which interest @ 9% shall be paid by the Discom.
The above instructions should be brought to the notice of all concerned for careful and
meticulous compliance.

5.2 Technical feasibility for the Rooftop solar connections - Compliance of
Electricity (Rights of Consumers) Amendment Rules, 2024. (Sales Circular No. USolar-
12/2024)

  In pursuance to Electricity (Rights of Consumers) Amendment Rules, 2024 the
Nigam has decided to do away the requirement of carrying out technical feasibility for Grid
Connected Roof Top Solar applications upto 10 Kwp with immediate effect.
 2.   The relevant portion of the said rules are reproduced as below for ready
reference:-
“(7) For installation of roof top solar photo voltaic systems, the technical feasibility study shall
be completed within a period of fifteen days and the outcome of the study shall be intimated
to the applicant, failing which it shall be presumed that the proposal is technically feasible.
(7A) The applications for roof top solar photo voltaic systems upto 10 kW capacity, complete
in all respects shall be deemed to have been accepted without requiring technical feasibility
study and any commensurate enhancement of the sanctioned load of the consumer, as may
be required, shall be carried out by the distribution licensee.”
(9) After installation of Roof Top Solar Photo Volatic System, the consumer shall submit the
installation certificate to such distributions licensee and such distributions licensee shall
complete signing of connection agreement, installations of meter and successful
commissioning of the Roof Top Solar Photo Volatic System with in fifteen days from the date
of submission of the certificate.
(9A) The formats of connections agreement and installation certificate shall be placed on web
portal of the distributions licensee.”
3).   Chief Engineer IT, UHBVN, Panchkula shall make necessary changes in the
UHBVN Solar Portal regarding the same.
4). The concerned SDO (OP) shall maintain the record of each distribution transformer on
which solar connections have been released and will augment/provide additional
transformer as and when required.
5).   It shall be the responsibility of the concerned Superintending Engineer (OP) to
monitor and ensure the adherence of the said directions at their respective circle.
6).   Sales Circular No. U-29/2021 is amended to the above extent and Sales
Circular No. U-05/2024 is superseded.
   The above instructions should be brought to the notice of all concerned for
strict and meticulous compliance with immediate effect.

5.3 Regarding supply of solar power on RESCO mode by installation and
commissioning of Grid Connected Rooftop Solar Power Plants with Net metering
facility in various Jails and other Govt. buildings.( Sales Instruction No. U- 02/2019)

Kindly refer to Memo No. Ch-22/CE/HPPC/Solar/Prison dated 03.04.2019 vide which it
was decided to allow installation of RTSPPs under RESCO mode at premises of 18 (10
belongs to UHBVN), Jails of the Prison Deptt. for supply to respective Jails through Net
Meter in terms of Regulation 61 of the Haryana Electricity Regulatory Commission (Terms
and Conditions for Determination of Tariff from Renewable Energy Sources, Renewable
Purchase Obligation and Renewable Energy Certificate) Regulations 2017 subject to any
amendment in the relevant HERC Regulations from time to time. As per the said Regulation,
the RESCO can supply/provide the power for the captive use of the premises where the
system is installed along with net meter and can sell the remaining power to HPPC on the
minimum last tariff discovered and conveyed by HPPC as per the HERC Regulations.
Regulation 61 of the HERC RE Regulations, 2017 is reproduced below for ready reference:-
“The rooftop space available in the government organization, institutions, buildings or vacant
land of the same can also be provided on lease/rent to the Independent Power Producer/
RESCO developer for setting up of solar power projects.
For such sites the lease/rent rate shall be decided by a Committee of Deputy Commissioner
of concerned district, PWD (B&R) Department and the Department owning the building. The
developer can also supply/provide the power for the captive use of the premises
where the system is installed along with net meter and can sell the remaining power
to HPPC on the minimum last tariff discovered and conveyed by HPPC or to third
party as per the HERC Regulations.”
  As intimated by CE/HPPC, the minimum last tariff discovered through
competitive bidding for procurement of 400 MW solar power by HPPC through SECI, which
has also been approved by HERC vide its Order dated 27.02.2019, is Rs.2.44 per kWh.
  Accordingly, any surplus power exported to the grid remaining unadjusted
under net metering shall be paid @ Rs.2.44 per kWh by way of adjustment in the
subsequent bills of the consumer by the concerned XEN ‘OP’.

5.4 Installation, testing & sealing of net meter – clarification thereof.( Sales

5.5 The Haryana Electricity Regulatory Commission (Rooftop Solar Grid
Interactive System based on Net Metering) Regulation, 2014 - Implementation
procedure thereof (Sales Circular No. U- 43 /2017)

Simplified procedure for implementation of Haryana Electricity Regulatory Commission
(Rooftop Solar Grid Interactive System based on Net Metering) Regulation, 2014 was
circulated vide Sales circular No. U-39/2016. Now Director, Renewable Energy Department,
Haryana has issued guidelines regarding installation of the grid connected solar power
plant in the state (2017-18) vide memo no. DRE/2017/1147-67 dated Panchkula, the
01.06.2017 wherein inter-alia it is stipulated as under:-
  For best synchronization of the GCRT solar power plant with the grid
power, three phase solar inverter shall be installed with the solar power plant if
synchronized with the three phase grid supply. Similarly, single phase solar inverter
shall be installed with the solar power plant if synchronized with the single phase
grid supply. The Rated Capacity of the Inverter/PCU shall not be less than the solar
PV array capacity subject to variation of 5%.
  Accordingly, it has been decided as under:-
1. GCRT solar power plant installed by consumers under net metering and having three
phase supply from the Nigam should install three phase solar inverter only.
2. GCRT solar power plant installed by consumers under net metering and having single
phase supply from the Nigam should install single phase solar inverter only.

5.6 The Haryana Electricity Regulatory Commission (Rooftop Solar Grid
Interactive System based on Net Metering) Regulation, 2014- Implementation
procedure thereof. (Sales Circular No. U- 36/2017)

Please refer to Sales Circular No. U-13/2017 vide which instructions regarding submission
of safety certificate by the applicant in case of installation of Rooftop Grid Connected Solar
Power Project has been issued.
  In view of the clarification received from CEI/GoH, it has been decided that
Solar Power Generating units upto 100 KVA capacity are not required to be inspected by
Electrical Inspector or Chartered Electrical Safety Engineer.
  The Sales Circular No. U-13/2017 has been superseded and S.I. U-03/2016
and 39/2016 stands amended to the above extent.

6.3 Single Point to Supply to Residential Colonies or Office cum Residential
Complexes of Employers, Group Housing Societies and Commercial cum Residential
Complexes of Developers, Regulations. (Sales Circular No. U-4/2014)

Please refer to Sales Circular No.U-07/2013 dated 01.02.2013 was issued in compliance to
the HERC notification dated 09.01.2013 vide which the detailed guidelines for single point
supply were circulated. Now, it has been decided that all Power Colonies (having more than
20 nos. houses) to be issued bills on Single Point Metering w.e.f. 01.04.2014.
  The procedure for implementation of the regulation are as under please.
  The procedure for implementation of supply of electricity on single point is to
be completed by 30th January.
1) All Head of the State Power Utilities/BBMB/Power grid shall issue directions for
appointment of Nodal Officer for the colonies under their jurisdiction.
2) The designated officer’s names be intimated to the office of CGM/Commercial DH/UH
concerned by 15th January.
3) The Nodal officer will map the colony on the enclosed format-1 by 30th January and
will hand over to the SDO (OP) concerned.
4) The SDO (OP) will got prepared a separate meter blank as per the list supplied by the
Nodal officer.
5) The bills will be issued as usual in the month of February/ March and the final
reading in the bills of February/ March 2014 will also be supplied to the Nodal officer and
that meter reading will be entered in the meter blanks as IR. for the next bills.
6) All the meters in that colony will be read on the same day in the month of
February/March and simultaneously reading of Single Point meter will be recorded.
7) On First April, the reading of Single Point Meter and all meters will be read
simultaneously.

359

8) On the basis of reading of 1st April, the bills of Single Point Supply and consumers
will be generated, will be issued by 7th April and to be distributed by 10th of April.
9) All residents have to deposit their bills to the Nodal Officer by 17th April and the Nodal
Officer will deposit Single Point bill to the SDO (OP) by 25th April.
Initially the SDO (OP) will provide services for:-
1) Preparation of Meter Blank as per survey to be submitted by the Nodal officer.
2) Preparation of bill on the reading to be submitted by Nodal Officer.
3) Mtc. of the LD system and Distribution transformer.
4) Replacement of any defective meter on deposit of meter cost by the Nodal officer.
5) The facility for testing of individual meters for accuracy/tempering or
calibration/sealing on the request of Nodal officer.

SECTION 7 RELAESE OF CONNECTION IN UN-AUTHORISED COLONIES

7.1  Release of electricity connections in un-authorized colonies and slums.
(Sales Circular No. U-26/2023).

  Haryana Electricity Regulatory Commission (HERC) has notified 3rd
Amendment to HERC Electricity Supply Code Regulation, 2014 which states as under:-
2.  The following para shall be added below the clause 4.4.1(5)
“That facility of electricity connection may be provided to those who are residing in un-
authorized colonies / Slums without insisting on ownership / legal occupancy proof;
Provided further, release of electricity connection shall not in any way confer upon the
consumer any lawful ownership/legal occupancy rights on the property. The connection
has been released and meter has been installed with a clear understanding that it is solely
for the purpose of meter reading to ensure generation of bill as per consumption and does
not create any ownership/ legal occupancy rights over the property.”
3.  An affidavit (Annex-I) as well as indemnity bond (Annex-II) shall be taken from
each of such consumer stating clearly that he shall be liable for any legal action relating to
the said premises by the department/agency concerned, namely, Local Bodies Department
or Town and Country Planning Department or Panchayat Department or any other legal /
competent authority as the case may be.
4.  XENs (OP) will apprise the details of connections released under this circular
to the concerned authorities’ viz. the Commissioner or Executive Officer of Municipal
Corporation or Municipal Council or Secretary of the Municipal Committee or E.O. HSVP
or BDPO at the end of every month.
5.  A separate code “NOP” shall be reflected upon energy bills of such
prospective consumers for easy identification.
6.  The Sales Circular No. U-02/2020 is amended to the extent of 3rd
Amendment mentioned above (copy of which is enclosed for ready reference). The Sales
Circular No. U-32/2017 is hereby superseded.
  The above instructions should be brought to the notice of all concerned for
careful and meticulous compliance.

Relevant Clause in Duty to supply electricity on request, Power to recover
