17.2 Nodal agency:- The office of Joint Director/Deputy Director of District shallAct as
Nodal agency of the District level clearance committee of the concerned District.

430

17.3 The District Level Clearance Committee shall consider the applications for
clearances submitted by an investor for 45 services mentioned in Annexure 1 of the
notification.

18 Composite Application form (CAF), processing and monitoring of CAF
1. Every applicant seeking to apply for clearances required for establishment or
operation of an Industry mentioned in Annexure 1 of notification shall apply through online
portal of Department of Industries. The CAF of the project upto the investment of Rs. 10
crore or CLU cases upto 1 acre in conforming zone will be sent online to the Nodal agency
of the concerned District and the relevant part of the same shall be sent by Nodal agency
to the concerned authority/ office for necessary clearance/approval/ report on the same
day or on second day after its receipt.
2. The authority shall process the application and send its orders sanctioning or
rejecting the application, as the case may be, to the nodal agency so that the same can be
given to the applicant.
3. The authority may ask for additional information from the applicant within 7 days
only through the nodal agency and with its approval.
4. The concerned department shall delegate the concurrent powers under their
respective Acts/ Rules/Orders through specific notification to the officers of the department
posted at the district headquarter as an Empowered Officer to grant
clearances/sanction/NOC/certificates at par with the competent authority of the
department except the approvals/sanction, currently being granted at the level of CM and
for those services wherein, powers are vested with the elected body/council.
5. The time limit shall be applicable from the date of the additional information has
been furnished by the applicant for approval of clearance by the concerned authority.
6. In case the application is rejected or approved with modifications by the authority
than DLCC shall examine such orders passed by the authority and if the committee
considers that there are valid grounds for a change in such decisions, it shall take a decision
which shall be binding on the authority as per 11(1) of the Haryana Industrial Promotion
Act,2005.
7. The deemed clearance certificate shall be issued by the Member-Secretary of District
Level Clearance Committee on the approval of DLCC in such cases wherein the clearances
are not issued within the prescribed period as per 11.1 of Haryana Industrial Promotion
Act,2005.
8. In case the clearance of the particular services is not provided within time limit as
prescribed in the annexure-1 annexed with the notification i.e. time prescribed 30 days for
all three stages of the 45 services then the applicant may opt to file complaint against the
authority of the concerned department under Right to Service Act,2015 by which the
clearance was to be issued. The State Govt. has already notified 119 such services under
the Right to Service Act,2015.

19 Meeting of District Level Clearance Committee.
1. The District Level Clearance Committee shall meet at least once in a week at district
headquarters or at such other place as the Chairman may specify from time to time to
transact its business and it can meet more than 1 time if the work load requires so.
2. Details of all the Composite Application Forms received from entrepreneurs prior to

431

the ensuing meeting shall be placed before the DLCC.
3. The Member Secretary shall by issuing a meeting notice, convene a meeting of district
Level Clearance Committee indicating the date, time and place of the meeting. He shall
enclose agenda and notes highlighting therein details of the applications cleared,
application cleared with modifications, rejected, information regarding the date on which
application deemed to have been approved in the case of deemed approvals and other
observations, if any received from the authority for the transaction of business in the said
meeting.
4. Member-Secretary shall also communicate the date, time place of the meeting to the
entrepreneurs, whose cases are included in the agenda.
5. All the members and invitees of the District Level Clearance Committee shall attend
the meeting in person and shall not depute their representatives.
6. The District Level Clearance Committee shall examine all the proposals places before
it and take appropriate decisions.
7. The Member – Secretary of the Committee shall within three days circulate the
proceedings of the meeting after taking approval of the Chairman.
8. Within two days of circulation of the proceedings of the meeting, the Member-
Secretary shall communicate the decision of the Committee to the authorities and the
entrepreneur concerned.
9. The authority shall grant or issue the necessary clearances within three days of the
Committee.

20 Deemed Clearance.
1. In case of applications pending with authorities concerned beyond the time limit, the
committee shall examine all such applications and pass orders forissuance of deemed
clearance which shall be binding on the authorities as per11(1) of Haryana Industrial
Promotion Act,2005.
2. As per the provision of Chapter 4 of para 4.1.2 of Haryana Enterprises Promotion
Policy-2015 all the clearances shall be delivered within 30 days for all 3 stages mentioned
in the annexure-1 appended to the notification except wherein the clearances are required
from Government of India.
3. The certificate of deemed clearance shall be issued by the nodal agency of DLCC in
the certificate of deemed clearance annexed as Annexure ‘A’

Section-14 Shifting of HT/ LT lines & Meters

14.1 Regarding Shifting of Electrical infrastructure while widening of village
Phirnies. ( Sales Circular No. U-11/2024).
  In reference to Sales Circular No. U-10/2024 dated 23.04.2024, certain
amendments are required. Henceforth, the following instructions shall be followed
regarding the shifting of electrical infrastructure during the widening of village phirnies:
2.  The department of Panchayati Raj, Haryana is undertaking the project of
paving and widening of village phirnis in the State. At some locations, the Electricity poles
are coming in between the RoW of phirni/road and are required to be shifted towards outer
edge.
3.  Matter was deliberated in the meeting of administrative secretaries of
Department of Energy and Panchayati Raj, Haryana held on 22.04.2024 and following
decisions were taken:-
(i) On the request of Panchayati Raj department, the electric lines/Poles existing on
village phirni causing hindrance in widening of the phirni to the proper width/RoW are
required to be shifted after framing of deposit estimate.
(ii) 11 meters poles will be erected for shifting of HT/LT lines so that, if needed, they can
be used to mount streetlights if requested by Development & Panchayat Department
/Panchayats. The shifting of poles/lines should be carried out by the Nigam without
insisting for prior deposition of the cost of shifting. Thereafter, the HDUs will raise the claim
with Development and Panchayats Department. Panchayats Department will send the
proposal to Government for releasing a separate budget. The Haryana DISCOMs can also
adjust the cost of shifting against the panchayat tax payable to respective panchayats as
per 2021 circular.
4.  Sales Circular No. U-10/2024 is superseded.
5.  These instructions be brought to the notice of all concerned for careful and
meticulous compliance.
……………………………………………………………………………………………………………………

14.2 Removal of dangerous poles coming in the middle of road for general
safety of passerby. (Sales Circular No. U-01/2023)

The instructions on the above subject issued vide Sales Circular No. Ushifting –
15/2022 are modified as under pursuant to decision of Board of Directors: -
   It has been observed that at some locations, electricity poles have come in the
middle of main roads/approach roads which may be due to widening of road or construction
of new roads. These have been constructed or widened by Govt. Agencies and entire cost of
shifting is usually deposited with the Nigam offices. Somehow these individual poles have
not been shifted, thus, creating hindrance to movement of public and vehicles which can
be a cause of road accidents especially in the night hours. Similarly, due to repeated
repair/construction of roads, the vertical via of electrical lines has also reduced making the
spot prone to electrical accident.

2.  Now, keeping in view the safety of public and vehicle movements on road, it

438

has been decided that SDOs (OP) shall identify all such places and undertake shifting as
per following procedure: -
(i) For the sites/locations where upto 2 poles are to be shifted from the middle of the
road, SDO (OP) concerned shall frame deposit estimate for shifting of such poles and get it
sanctioned from the competent authority.
Thereafter a notice shall be sent to the concerned office like
NHAI/PWD/B&R/MC/Marketing Board etc. for deposition of the cost of estimate within
fifteen days.
In case the amount is not deposited by the concerned department, the work of shifting shall
be carried out by SDO (OP) for general safety of passersby and actual cost of such shifting
shall be recovered through the electricity bill of concerned department.
(ii) or the sites/locations where more than 2 but up to 5 poles are to be shifted from the
middle of the road, the concerned XEN (OP) shall mandatorily visit the site and if finds that
such poles are accident prone to the vehicles and general public shall direct SDO (OP)
concerned in writing for undertaking the shifting of these poles.
On receipt of such directions, SDO(OP) shall frame deposit estimate for shifting of such
poles and get it sanctioned from the competent authority.
Thereafter a notice shall be sent to the concerned office like
NHAI/PWD/B&R/MC/Marketing Board etc. for deposition of the cost of estimate within
fifteen days.
In case the amount is not deposited by the concerned department, the work of shifting shall
be carried out by SDO (OP) for general safety of passersby and actual cost of such shifting
shall be recovered through the electricity bill of concerned department.
(iii) For the sites/locations where above 5 poles are to be shifted from the middle of the
road, the concerned SE (OP) shall mandatorily visit the site and if finds that such poles are
accident prone to the vehicles and general public shall direct SDO (OP) through XEN (OP)
concerned in writing for undertaking the shifting of these poles.
On receipt of such directions, SDO (OP) shall frame deposit estimate for shifting of such
poles and get it sanctioned from the competent authority.
Thereafter a notice shall be sent to the concerned office like
NHAI/PWD/B&R/MC/Marketing Board etc. for deposition of the cost of estimate within
fifteen days.
In case the amount is not deposited by the concerned department, the work of shifting shall
be carried out by SDO (OP) for general safety of passersby and actual cost of such shifting
shall be recovered through the electricity bill of concerned department.
(iv) However, in case of Panchayats where petty/road/street construction works are
going and there is pole hindrance or any accident prone pole is there, the same be shifted
at Nigam’s cost after getting written request from SDOs/XENs, Panchyati Raj also in
addition to BDPO, DDPO, ADC.

3.  In the first instance, 15 days will be given to SDO ‘OP’ to identify such sites.
Thereafter, a 7 days notice shall be given to the Govt. agency (who has executed the
widening/creation/repairing of road like NHAI/PWD B&R/MC/Marketing Board) for
deposition of cost of work. In case no response is received, work of shifting of such pole(s)
or maintaining height of electrical line causing hindrance shall be executed by the Sub-
Division itself and amount/expenses incurred in such work shall be charged in the energy
bills of the concerned department.

439

4.  Sub-Division shall ensure to complete the work of shifting within 45 days.

5.  The circulars shall remain in force. As and when, any such dangerous site is
created, SDO ‘OP’ shall exercise these powers in very interest of general public.
6.   The Sales Circular No. U-15/2022 is hereby superseded.
   The above instructions should be brought to the notice of all concerned for
careful and meticulous compliance with immediate effect.

14.3 Regarding expenditures (for shifting of cables/ lines, any electrical
infrastructure installed by UHBVN) related to execution/ development of any facility
(creation of any sub- station/store, augmentation/extension of the station/power
plants etc.) by HVPNL/HPGCL. (Sales Instruction No. U- 01/2023).

  Regarding subject cited above, Nigam has decided as under:-
"Any expenditures (for shifting of cables/lines, any electrical infrastructure installed by
UHBVN) related to execution/development of any facility (creation of any sub-station/store,
augmentation/extension of the sub- station/power plants etc.) by HVPNL/HPGCL shall be
borne by UHBVN as aim of creation of these facility is to provide reliable power supply to
Nigam's consumer. Further, if borne by other Power Utilities (HVPNL/HPGCL), the same
shall be passed on to UHBVN as part of ARR."
  The above instructions should be brought to the notice of all concerned for
strict and meticulous compliance.

14.5.1 Instructions for shifting of 33 kV lines. (Sales Instruction No. U-

Now, the matter has again been deliberated and decided that the shifting of 33 KV lines
shall be approved by WTDs through CE/PD&C, UHBVN, Panchkula. The other terms &
conditions to be followed are as under: -
1. In the first instance, the possibility of providing free passage corridor by the applicant
under the existing 33 kV line should be examined as per site conditions instead of shifting.
2. The memorandum for shifting of 33 kV line shall be signed with name & date by all
officer i.e. SE (OP), SE/Const & XEN (OP) / SDO (OP) concerned and the proposal shall be
routed through CE (OP) concerned who will examine and forward the same with
recommendation to the O/o CE/PD&C,UHBVN, Panchkula, then CE/PD&C will put-up the
case to the WTDs for approval.
3. SE (OP) & SE /Const. should certify on the sketch that they have personally checked
the site and found that the proposal for shifting of 33 kV line is genuine and technically
feasible.
4. As per site conditions, the aspect of durability of 33 kV line due to shifting be kept
in view.
5. Proposed line should be erected on lattice towers strictly as per Instruction
No.1/2020/PD&C issued by PD&C wing vide memo No. Ch-26/XEN/R-II/F-395 dated
11.05.2020 mentioning span lengths etc. with span length of 50 Mtr.
6. The U/G XLPE Cable should only be used if there is ROW problem and with double
circuit (free passage) under the trench / through horizontal direction drilling method
(trenchless boring) quality of PN 10 or PN 10 having PE-63 grades shall be mention & 4
runs single core 33 kV XLPE Cable of size 630 Sq mm in HDPE pipe and undertaking from
the applicant should be obtained on affidavit that he would never carry out any type of
construction over the proposed route of such shifting.
7. Span wise length of proposed shifting and the length of spans to be dismantled
should be mentioned on the sketch with size of ACSR along with name of feeding end and
receiving end substation. Sketch with clear dimension of land of applicant be superimposed
on approved layout plan along with status of adjoining and 8 Nos. coloured copies on A3
sheet be submitted duly signed with date & name of concerned officer (as per Sr. No. 2) &
consumer / applicant with all certificates mentioned there upon.
8. Undertaking on the affidavit should be taken from the applicant that he will bear the
total expenditure involved in the shifting.
9. The documentary proof in this regard i.e. approved building plan of the project, proof
of intention to start work/construction at site, CLU if any etc. should be attached along
with actual/authentic reasons of line shifting should be mentioned in the memorandum
and in the request application. The applicant’s signature may also be got appended on the
sketch.
10. The work of shifting will be carried out through SE/OP concerned.
11. Inspection of C.E.I Govt. of Haryana should be obtained before energization of the
proposed 33 kV line.
12. SDO (OP) S/Divn. concerned shall ensure deposit of full amount of the estimate by
the beneficiary before start of the work.
13. Right of way problem shall lie in the scope of beneficiary person desirous of such
work. It will be upto him to take care of this problem.
14. Work will be taken in hand only after sanctioning the deposit estimate by the
Competent Authority and observing all other formalities required as per Nigam’s
instructions.

443

15. All the material (usable & unusable) will be returned to the store immediately after
dismantlement and usable material will be used and unusable material will be declared
scrap for disposal.
16. Labour charges of dismantled existing 33 kV line along with loading, un-loading &
transportation of the dismantled material from site to Divisional/Central Store shall be
included in the estimate.
17. The 33 kV line will be erected as per the latest instructions of Indian Electricity Rules
as adopted by Nigam.
18. If self execution is opted by the applicant, work will be carried out through approved
vendor/contractor as per the latest instructions of Nigam.
19. The material for work under self-execution scheme shall be dealt as per the existing
instructions of the Nigam.
20. Line shall be energized only after joint Inspection and clearance from the Committee
of S.E/OP, SE/ Const and XEN’OP’ concerned and finally from CEI.
Sale Instruction No. U-05/2015 is superseded.

Shifting of Meter Outside the Premise.

14.6 Shifting of the meter outside the premises
14.6.1 Shifting of Urban Domestic Meters outside the premises.( Sales Circular
No. U- 22/2017)

It has been observed that there is stiff resistance from some consumers in the urban area
at the time of relocation of meters from inside the consumer premises to outside.
2. One of the reasons of consumer resistance on relocation of meters is the fact that the
meters which are found tampered / with fake seals are got checked in the M&T lab and
there after theft penalty is imposed as per the M&T lab report.
3. However, it is worth mentioning that at this stage the meters which are still existing
inside the premises are those which were installed several years ago. In between there might
have occurred change of tenancy / ownership. There is every likely hood that some of the
innocent consumers might be getting penalised due to some acts of tempering etc. done in
the past which was not in the knowledge of present occupier of the premises.
4. To redress such issues, it has been decided to give one time relaxation to such
consumers as per the below given terms & conditions:
i) This relaxation will be given to the consumers located on the feeders where sizeable
chunk of meters (say 30%) is still inside the premises and there is a drive by the department
to shift out the meters on the feeder.
ii) Such feeder will be identified by S.E. ‘OP’ by 30.06.2017 so that such relief is
provided only to consumers on those feeders. The list of feeders mentioning approximate
percentage of left out meters will be circulated by him to his subordinate offices and
commercial wing as well.
iii) In all such cases, the packed meter will be got duly tested from M&T lab to find out
the acts of tampering. The amount of theft penalty will be worked out and a notice will be
issued to the consumer that his meter has been found tampered etc. which has been noted
by the Nigam and that his behaviour is not upto the mark. However, a gesture of goodwill
no action will be taken by the Nigam in the hope that the consumer will desist from such
acts in future.
 All relevant Sale Circulars / Instructions in this regard stand superseded.

14.7 Shifting of meters of Nigam employees outside the premises (Sales
Instruction No. U-04/2017)

It has been brought in the notice of management that some of the consumers who are
resisting shifting of meter outside their premises are advancing the argument that let the
Nigam shift the meters outside the premises of its own employees first and thereafter, the
Nigam can shift their meter also. It has, therefore, been decided by the management that
all the employees should get the meters shifted outside the premises at their own initiative
for the connection in their/ family members name or the connection from which the
electricity supply is being availed. Work of getting the meter shifted should be completed
by 30.04.2017.
  Accordingly, all the employees working in your respective offices should be
instructed to get their meters shifted outside the premises in line with above directive. If
the meter of any employee is found not shifted outside his premises, it will attract the
disciplinary action against the employee himself.

446

14.7.1 Standardization of work of shifting of meters outside the premises.(
Sales Circular No. U- 48/2016)

Please refer to S.C. No. U-06/2015 dated 07.04.2015 vide which the guidelines for
installation of meters during relocation outside the consumer premises were issued.
Now, during the field visits by various Nodal officers it has come to notice that the work of
shifting of meters outside the premises is not being done properly and various deficiencies
are being noted regarding the workmanship after each visit. To have a uniform working on
L.R.P. and MGJG. The following guidelines be followed by each office:-
1.  The meter should be installed on pole only (except in a very exception case on the
wall) at a height of maximum 6 ½ feet top of the meter box and lower height 4 ½ feet from
the ground so that meter reading is visible and can be taken easily.
2.  The meters be placed in one-in-one box or Four in one box only having provision of
installation of optical probes, depending upon site conditions. In case of narrow streets, the
four-in-one box be used and installed on the pole at the entrance of the street. In this way
incoming supply will be restricted at the entrance and outgoing (may be lengthy) be
provided to each house.
 Three phase MCB should not be used for installation of Three no Single phase meter
as optical port will not be taken out outside the box for each meter.
3.  All old Iron sheet MCB (purchased & supplied by consumers) are to be replaced as
they are not having provision of installation of optical probes.
4.  The incoming cable provided on the pole should be individual for each consumer and
that too be armoured.
5.  Outgoing cable should be un-armoured one
6. All incoming cables i.e. armoured one should be bunched together from one side of
the pole.
7.  All outgoing cable i.e. un-armoured one should be bunched from other side of the
pole and should be kept min. 2 FT lower than the overhead conductor of LT line/LT AB
cable to avoid chances of un-authorized inter connection on the top of pole.
8.  The incoming armoured PVC should be peeled to the minimum extend for inserting
into the incoming side of the meter terminals as in case of long naked peeling, the very
purpose of armoured will be defeated as the same is suspectable to theft.
9.  While installing the meter it should be checked that the complete meter display
should
completely come in front of Glass of MCB and should not have any obstruction (It should
be done by adjusting the meter up or down with the provision provided in the MCB).
10.  The meter should be fixed by tightening both screws (meter gets tilted in case one
screw is left loose or un-provided).
11. The incoming and outgoing PVC be fully tightened in the meter terminals to avoid
chances of meter burnt due to looseness.
12.  Meter Terminal Covers be fixed and sealed properly by JE/AFM in-charge.
13.  The optical eye be fixed on the meter and its optical port be affixed on the slot
provided on MCB with the help of both the screws. Providing one screw will be useless as

447

while inserting the knob of CMRI (Cable), port could be pushed back in the MCB or damage
the contact points.
14.  MCB cover be fitted properly and it should be checked from all sides and then both
seal be provided on the MCB.
15.  Account number of the consumer be written on the MCB's lower portion as well as
on the meter inside the MCB by permanent marker.
16.  Account wise detail of the meter with serial No. provided be maintained by the JE/
AFM In-charge.
17.  LT /AB cable is to be used for replacing of ACSR only in those area where case of
direct hooking is suspected. Also the size of L.T./AB cable to be used be decided as per the
no. of consumer's and their load. The current carrying capacity of each size is as under:-
Size 16-25 25-25 35-25 50-35 95-70 120-70
Cable Current
carrying capacity
(Amp).
60 76 92 110 155 180

18.  The termination from LT/AB cable should be made through junction boxes. Also the
load balancing on each phase has to be done during this meter shifting process. This can
be done as under:-
(i)  One phase be terminated on 1st pole and all the connection be connected on that
phase and 2nd phase be terminated on 2nd pole and all the connection be connected on
that phase and 3rd phase likewise be terminated.
      Or
(ii)  All the three phase terminated on each pole and number of connections on each
phase be connected after counting their connected load.
19.  If the junction box are not used then termination of LT/AB cable be sealed with m-
seal i.e. there should not be any naked termination from LT/AB Cable.
20.  The spared PVC and spared MCBs are to be dismantled from the sites which is not
being done in many field offices presently, which may also cause theft of energy by that
spared PVC. All the dismantled material returned to store.
21.  In very exceptional cases only the meter should be installed on the wall in such a
manner that incoming cable should be tied to hinge below the projection of roof of the
premises that cannot be easily accessible to the consumer.

14.8 Conversion of feeding source from Rural to Urban mode viz-a-viz
redefining of MC limits (Sales Instruction No. U-12/2015)

  Please refer to S.I. No. U-09/2015 dated 04.09.2015 vide which guidelines
were circulated regarding providing Urban mode supply to the areas

448

(villages/town/localities) falling within the redefined Municipal limit. Now, the amended
guidelines in compliance to the decision of MDs Coordination Committee meeting held on
18.08.2015 are as under please.

a. The expenditure relating to the Distribution system shall be borne by the respective
distribution utility and expenditure relating to transmission system shall be borne by
the HVPNL. The expenditure in this regard be recovered through Capex.
b. All the defective meters / electro mechanical meters shall be replaced with electronic
meters and installed outside the premises.
c. HVDS /LVDS shall be provided as required.

h. No tube well connection would be permitted on the feeder.
i. HT meter shall be provided to monitor the AT&C losses for every village/feeder.

The supply on Urban mode shall commence after competition of aforesaid works, especially
relocation of meters outside the houses, installation of AB cables and energy accounting
measures.

14.9 Conversion of Existing LT Bulk Supply Consumers with load above 70
KW to HT supply (Sales Circular No.U-41/2006)

As per prevailing instructions of the Nigam reiterated vide S.C. No.4/2001 dated
11.1.2001 all new connections to Bulk Supply Consumers having load more than 70 KW
are to be released on HT pressure of supply.

 It has been decided by the Nigam that all existing Bulk Supply Connections having
load of 71 KW and above should be converted into HT pressure of supply. A period of 6
months may be allowed through a notice to the consumers for changing over the supply
from LT to HT by making their own arrangements for the transformer and allied switchgear.
It may be clearly indicated in the notice that in case, a consumer fails to comply with the
above instructions within the stipulated period, his supply will be disconnected.

15.2 SOP for Redressal of public grievances regarding erroneous/disputed
bills. (Sales Circular No. U- 16/2022)

Earlier Sales Circular No.U-43/2012 dated 27.12.2012 was issued by Nigam for the
settlement of the consumer billing disputes w.r.t connected and PDCO cases.
Subsequently, HERC Electricity Supply Code Regulations 2014 was circulated by Nigam
having the following enabling provisions for dealing with the matters related to
erroneous/disputed billing:

 Clause No. 6.10.4:- If the licensee establishes during review or otherwise or as a
result of audit observation that a consumer has been under-charged, a 15 days notice shall
be served upon the consumer to enable him to contest the demand. However, in case of
additional demand being made out by internal audit in respect of any consumer, the officer
concerned shall satisfy himself in the matter before giving notice to the consumer. After receipt
of reply from the consumer, the licensee shall review the amount charged after taking into
account the facts submitted by the consumer. For the amount which is chargeable, after
considering reply of the consumer, the licensee shall recover the amount without levy of
surcharge from the consumer by issuing a separate bill and in such cases at least 30 days
shall be given to the consumer to pay the bill. In case the consumer fails to pay the bill by the
due date, he shall be liable to pay, in addition, surcharge for the period of delay.

 Clause No.6.10.6:-While communicating the decision on the review of the bill, the

451

licensee shall advise the consumer in writing his right to prefer an appeal against the decision
of the licensee to Consumer Grievance Redressal Forum.

Furtherance to the above, HERC has also issued Regulation No. HERC/48/2020/1st
Amendment/2022 for providing guidelines to the Licensees for establishment of Forum for
Redressal of Grievances of the consumers; for appointment of Ombudsman; for
representation against non-redressal of grievances of consumers and the time and manner
of settlement of grievances by Ombudsman and for matters incidental and ancillary thereto.
In compliance to the above regulations, further Sales Circular No. UReg-09/2022 dated
06.07.2022 has also been issued by Nigam besides the notification issued by the O/o
CE/Admn. vide memo no Ch-76/UH/GA-218/Vol-III/cadre dated 18.08.2022 w.r.t. the
constitution of Circle Forum/Zonal Forum/ Corporate Forum.
Instances have been observed that the matters related to redressal of public grievances
regarding erroneous/disputed bills are not being dealt and expedited in letter spirit of the
enabling instructions/regulations. Such practice not only causes undue harassment to the
consumers but also lead to undue accumulation of amount not getting realized in time.
In view of above, it has been observed that there is an immediate need to issue/reiterate
necessary SOP/guidelines for the stakeholders, to the extent of the enabling provisions
stipulated under HERC Supply Code Regulation Clause No. 6.10.4 and 6.10.6, Sales
Circular No. U-09/2022 and notification issued by the office of CE/Admn. vide memo no
Ch-76/UH/GA-218/Vol-III/cadre dated 18.08.2022, for dealing with the matter of
erroneous/disputed billing in letter & spirit of the existing instructions/regulation.

   As such, the following SOP/guidelines are being issued to mitigate such
instances from happening and to evolve best practice for dealing with the instant matter of
under charging (barring cases of theft of electricity, unauthorized use of electricity, where
the consumer is found at fault for damage to meter & apparatus and matters related to
Open Access granted under the Electricity Act, 2003) to any consumer if establishes during
review or otherwise or because of audit observation:-
i. Internal Audit Party (IAP)/Audit Team/M&P/Vigilance wing and any other designated
office/officer/official of Nigam shall be authorized to check/review/inspect/audit the
commercial business activities/operations in sub-division/field offices on periodic
basis or otherwise.
ii. The IAP/Audit Team of Nigam, during the checking/inspection/audit of the sub-
division/field offices, shall establish any under-charging to the consumer strictly as per
the Nigam’s Instructions in vogue and shall prepare a detailed assessment report in the
matter only after thorough due diligence and verification of the facts from record/details
to be made available by the concerned officer in-charge (SDO/JE-I/JE)/official
(CA/UDC/LDC) of the sub-division/field offices.
iii. However, in case of checking/inspection carried out by M&P/Vigilance wing and any
other designated office/officer/official of Nigam, any under charging/loss of revenue
(LOR) to the consumer shall be assessed by the officer/official in-charge of the
concerned sub-division/field offices and SDO-CBO/(Audit Team-CBO) based on the
checking/inspection report received in the matter from the authorized team. It shall be
ensured that any assessment for under charging/LOR is done strictly as per the
Nigam’s Instructions and with proper scrutiny & verification of the facts/details from
the available record.

452

iv. The IAP/Audit Team, after preparing the report, shall hand over the same to the officer
in-charge of the concerned sub-division/field offices.
v. However, in the absence of the officer in-charge of the concerned sub-division/field
offices, the report may be handed over by the IAP/Audit Team to the CA/UDC in-charge
of the office.
vi. Within 10 working days of receipt of the reports w.r.t. the under charging/LOR
associated with consumer billing, the officer in-charge of the concerned sub-
division/field offices, along with his/her CA/UDC, will schedule a meeting
(physical/virtual) with SDO-CBO/(Audit Team-CBO) and together they will jointly
decide the acceptance or rejection of the reports/cases on merit and shall prepare a
detailed minutes of meeting in the matter. Further, SE/CBO shall approve the minutes
of meetings.
vii. The committee comprising of the officer in-charge of the concerned sub-division/field
offices, his/her CA/UDC and SDO-CBO/(Audit Team-CBO) shall examine the cases in
a legitimate manner in accordance with the Consumers’ billing record/case file and
Nigam’s Instructions in vogue in the matter.
Note: For Non-R-APDRP Offices being billed through HARTRON Platform, any decision
regarding the acceptance or rejection of the reports/cases shall be done by the officer in-
charge of the concerned sub-division/field offices, along with his/her
CA/UDC/CC/Official concerned in a similar manner.
viii. Further to the above decision w.r.t. the chargeable cases, the officer in-charge of the
concerned sub-division/field offices, in accordance with the provisions of HERC Supply
Code Regulation Clause No. 6.10.4, shall serve a 15 days’ notice (as per format attached
as Annexure-I) to the consumer to enable him to contest the demand.
ix. However, in case of additional demand being made out by IAP/Audit Team in respect
of any consumer, the officer in-charge of the concerned sub-division/field offices shall
satisfy himself in the matter before giving notice to the consumer.
x. Within 10 working days, after receipt of reply from the consumer alongwith the facts,
the committee, comprising of the officer in-charge of the concerned sub-division/field
offices, his/her CA/UDC and SDO-CBO/(Audit Team-CBO), shall consider the same
and review the amount charged/demand & further, decide the matter with the approval
of SE/SBO for the amount which is chargeable.
xi. Furtherance to the above, the officer in-charge of the concerned sub-division/field
offices shall recover the amount without levy of surcharge from the consumer by issuing
a separate bill, and in such case at least 30 days shall be given to the consumer to pay
the bill.
xii. In case the consumer fails to pay the bill by the due date, he/she shall be liable to pay,
in addition, surcharge for the period of delay.
xiii. While communicating the decision on the review of the bill, the officer in-charge of the
concerned sub-division/field offices shall advise the consumer in writing his/her right
to prefer an appeal against the above decision to Consumer Grievance Redressal Forum
(as defined vide HERC Regulation No. HERC/48/2020/1st Amendment/2022 and
circulated by Nigam vide Sales Circular No Ureg-09/2022 along with the notification
issued by the O/o CE/Admn. vide memo no Ch 76/UH/GA-218/Vol-III/cadre dated
18.08.2022 w.r.t. the constitution of Circle Forum/ Zonal Forum/Corporate Forum).

xiv. Any aggrieved consumer/ party can file his/her grievance, in writing to the Consumer
Grievance Redressal Forum following the procedure as defined in Clause No. 2.17 &

453

15.4 KNOW YOUR BILL” SCHEME (Sales Instruction No. U-02/2021)

It has come into the notice that there are large number of billing and metering related
issues/complaints of consumers due to which consumers face harassment. Accordingly,
the matter has been considered by the Nigam and it has been decided to launch the “Know
Your Bill” Scheme. The operational guidelines of the scheme are as under: -
1. On every Thursday, each SDO ‘OP’ will remain present in his/her office and redress
consumer grievances regarding electricity bills, metering, connection dispute and tariff etc.
from 10.00 AM to 02.00 PM. The complaints received shall be resolved on the spot to the
extent possible and the record shall be maintained. Strict directions are hereby given to
follow the instructions and follow the schedule. On this day, SDOs (OP) shall review all
pending billing/metering complaints and ensure resolution of all complaints with in
timeline fixed by HERC.
2. Every Saturday has been fixed for holding village level Darbar in the jurisdiction of
Sub-Division by the SDO ‘OP’ from 10.00 AM to 01.00 PM. SDO will take the sub-division
team of JE/CA/Ledger Clerk/Consumer Clerk etc. with him and redress the consumer
grievances pertaining to electricity bill, metering, connection dispute, tariff etc. on the spot
to the extent possible.
3. In exceptional cases, if SDO is not present then senior most JE will hold the village
Darbar.
4. XEN ‘OP’ concerned will head the village Darbar in any sub-division every fortnight
and similarly, SE ‘OP’ will hold village Darbar once in a month at circle level.
5. Wide publicity through print media, social media/SMS should be given to the
scheme.
6. SE ‘OP’/XEN ‘OP’ shall ensure that no meeting is fixed during the time
SDO(OP)/XEN(OP) is occupied with the scheme.
7. Concerned staff should also remain present during the above schedule so that site
verification, if any required could be carried out on the same day.
8. If any activity is required at the end of Commercial Bank Office (CBO), prompt action
and redressal within 24hrs shall be ensured by XEN/CBO. And, if the complaint requires
higher time in redressal like involving binder management, SDO(OP) shall inform the fact
to the complainant.
9. All out efforts be ensured to redress the complaints on the spot itself or at the most
within 24 hours and intimation be sent to concerned SE ‘OP’/XEN ‘OP’.
10. SE(OP)/XEN(OP) shall review pendency of complaints in each sub-division and
ensure the success of this scheme.

15.5 Haryana Swarn Jayanti Bijli Samities. (Sales Circular No. U-27/2016.)

  Enclosed please find herewith the copy of the Power Department, GOH

The above instructions may be brought to the notice of all concerned for strict
and meticulous compliance.

HARYANA GOVERNMENT
POWER DEPARTMENT
NOTIFICATION
No.16/26/2016-4P
The 22nd July, 2016
Electricity is basic need of all segments of society. In order to address various issues relating
to supply of electricity in all the 230 sub divisions of both the electricity distribution
companies (DISCOMs) of the State, the Government of Haryana has decided to constitute
"Haryana Swarn Jayanti Bijli Samities" in every Operation Sub Division of Uttar Haryana
Bijli Vitran Nigam and Dakshin Haryana Bijli Vitran Nigam Limited.
2.  The "Haryana Swarn Jayanti Bijli Samiti" will consist or the following members:
(i)  Representatives of Industrial Association & Traders-2 No
(ii) Representatives of Resident Welfare Association (Urban Area)/Rural Domestic
Consumers-2 No
(iii) Representatives of farmers (wherever applicable)-2 No
(iv) Women Representatives-2 No.
(v) Public Water Works department representative-1 No.
(vi) Representative from District Administration-1 No
(vii) Representative of concerned Chairman. Municipal Corporation/Council of
Committee k (in case of Urban Areas).
(viii) Concerned Zila Parishad Members (in case of Rural Areas).
(ix) Representative of Chairman, Panchayat Samities.
SDO of the Sub Division concerned will be convener of the Samiti.
3. The nominees as per S.No.2 above will be appointed by the Deputy Commissioner
concerned. All the members shall be ordinary residents of the area under the jurisdiction
of the Sub Division concerned. There will be only one nominee from one village.
4.  Meeting of the Samiti shall be held at-least once in two months and the same will be
convened by the SDO Operation concerned. The meetings will be held in the offices of SDO
Operation only.
5.  Standing agenda for discussion in the meeting of the Samiti shall be as follows:-
(i)  Status of power supply to various categories.
(ii)  Status of loading of network, new projects etc.
(iii)  Status of distribution and AT&C losses in the area.
(iv)  Consumer tariff and other commercial information.

458

(v)  Consumer Grievances Redressal.
Any other agenda can be discussed as proposed by any of the member of the concerned.
It shall be tried that the grievances of the consumers if any are redressed on the spot.
6.  A register for recording proceedings of the meetings of Samitis shall be maintained
by the SDO Operation. Issues raised as well as discussions held will be recorded in the
register. It shall be got signed from all the members who may be present in the meeting.
7.  A copy of the proceedings will be sent by the SDO to XEN and SE Operation of the
district, who in turn will compile the information relating to all the Operation Sub-divisions
under their charge. The S.E. Operation of the district will analyse the nature of grievances
being put forward and suggest policy level remedial measures to be taken by the
management.
8.  An expenditure upto Rs.2000 per meeting may be incurred for convening the meeting
of the Samiti, including expenditure on refreshments.
9.  The Government of Haryana further orders that S.E. Operation concerned of the
district will get the names of the members of various Samitis notified from the Deputy
Commissioner within 15 days, and first meeting of the Samiti shall be held within 30 days
of the issuance of this notification.

15.7 Implementation of EoDB recommendations regarding release of
connection within 7days/15days. (Sales Circular No. U- 20/2018)
For the promotion of industries and investment in the state, various measures have been
taken to facilitate the investors and ease of doing business. Moving further, and in line with
the recommendations under business reform action plan [BRAP] 2018, the process of
release of electricity connection by industries is further simplified to provide connection
within 7 days/15 days as per the following guidelines: -
(a) Wherever there is no requirement of augmentation or extension of system including
at the end of the applicant, the charged connection will be provided within 7 days from the
date of application, provided the applicant has submitted all requisite documents and
charges along with the application.
(b)  Wherever the release of connection involves laying of cable having crossing over road
or any other area for which permission is required from Govt. Agencies like PWD, ULB etc,
for such cases, the charged connection will be provided within 15 days from the date of
application.
(c) The metering equipment will be provided by Discoms.
(d) In other cases, where either applicant has not submitted his intent to have immediate
electricity connection or where Nigam is required to augment/create new infrastructure, in
such cases, the connection will be released within 7 days/15 days of readiness of consumer
or creation of infrastructure by Nigam as per above timelines.
(e) The guidelines for processing the application is given as under

(1) Application: - The applicant while submitting the application in online portal is also
required to upload his signed intent that he is ready to take the connection along with the
ownership proof and identity proof. In the intent, he has to undertake that he has installed
the complete machinery, executed wiring as per regulations and has self-certification or is
ready for CEI inspection, if applied voltage is above 33 KV.
(2) Category of application: - The applicants applying as above will be covered under
“Release of Connection - EoDB-industrial category”.
(3) Scrutiny of application & document: - The application particulars, documents
submitted by applicant will be scrutinized on the same day. For such applications wherever
documents are complete and there is no requirement of augmentation/ extension of
distribution system, all the charges be got deposited and seniority of the same will be
maintained under “cable connection” which will have overriding priority.
(4) Deficiency in documents & charges: - However, if the application particulars and
ownership & identity documents are not complete and complete charges have not been
deposited, the timelines will not be applicable.
(5) Feasibility study: - For facilitating the applicants, every sub-division office shall
maintain the updated status of loading of distribution network and substations. Any
applicant before applying the application can also voluntarily undertook the pre-feasibility
assessment of load availability in the network before applying of electricity connection.
(6) For the purpose of these guidelines, the spare capacity available due to natural load
flow in the network and created under normal Capex programme based on estimated load
growth in various areas, will be considered for release of connection.

(7) CEI Inspection: - Up to 33KV voltage level, no CEI inspection is required. For supply
voltage greater than 33 KV, the electrical inspector will undertake the inspection on the 3rd

462

day of application for which one day advance intimation will be given Electrical inspector
and applicant. In case the consumer fails to get the inspection of installation on the
designated time or after inspection it is found that his installation does not conforms to
regulations, in that case, the time lines of 7 days & 15 days will not be applicable.
(a) The name of service, designated officer & Appellate Authority for this service would
be as under: -

15.8 Implementation of recommendations of “Ease of Doing Business”. (Sales
Circular No. U- 04/2016)

The Government of India and State Government have launched the programme
of “Make in India” in a big way wherein various incentives and facilities have been given to
investors to come up with investment, which will overall boost the economy and the State.
For the purpose various guidelines have been framed by Department of Industry Promotion
and Policy (DIPP) for implementing the ease of business. The electricity connection is one
of the requirement for investors while establishing the business unit, for which he requires
temporary connection and thereafter for commencing the operations of business, the
regular connection is required by the investors and industries. Accordingly, for providing
facility to industries in having electricity connection following guidelines are hereby issued
to all concerned for its meticulous compliance.
(a) The charges required for release of connection have been specified in schedule of
general and miscellaneous charges, which is applicable by S.C. No.U-27/2011 wherein
following fixed service connection charges have been specified for industrial connections:-
Sr. No. Category Fixed service connection charges
1. LT industry Rs.500/KW

463

2. HT industry Rs.750/KVA of contract demand

These charges are to be recovered for all the industrial connections which could be
connected up to 300 meters of LT and 11 KV line. As such, in the industrial estates
developed by HSIIDC and other departments having adequate electrical infrastructure, the
above provisions may be publicized that for electricity connections, the department is
charging fixed cost as per details above, as no other infrastructure creation charge is
required to be deposited.
(b) The industrial state developers i.e. HSIIDC and other departments responsible for
developing industrial states should be directed to upgrade electrical infrastructure from
time to time as per the projected requirement so that industrial applicants in the industrial
state may avail connections after paying the fixed service connection charges as detailed
above.
(c) The details of fixed charges, Security and application processing and calculator are
also available on the website of UHBVN wherein the consumers can also calculate the
charges required for release of connection. The consumer can also pay the application
processing fee and the demand notice charges through online payment gateway could also
upload the application online along with the only 2 Nos. documents required for release of
connection.
(d) The timelines for release of connections have been specified in electricity supply code,
applicable vide S.C. No.U-15/2014. For implementing the Ease of Doing Business
recommendations, all the field officers are directed that for the industrial estates, the
complete loading of transformer, sketch of industrial areas be kept readymade in the
subdivision office and wherever electrical infrastructure is available, the applicant in
industrial area be allowed to deposit the charges, documents and certification of installation
through CEI/3rd party as applicable at the time of application.
(e) For such applicants in industrial areas, the service connection order should be
issued within 5 days and the connection should be release within 7 days as per the time
lines specified in HERC supply code.
(f) For any application in the green field i.e. outside industrial areas, the applicant has
to erect the infrastructure in advance by himself or through licensee on payment of charges
as per regulation during the temporary connection period under which his business
installation work is under progress, so that by the time his business operation commences,
the electrical infrastructure is also ready and the consumer gets electricity connection on
demand within 15 days. The above instructions may be publicized in all the industrial
states and developed by HSIIDC and industrial department.

16.2 ToD/ToU Tariff/Night-time Concessional Tariff for FY 2024-25. (Sales
Circular No. U-29/2024).

  HERC in Tariff Order dated 05 March, 2024 in Case No. HERC/PRO-69 of
2023 & HERC/PRO-70 of 2023 for FY 2024-25 has approved the Time of Day (ToD)/Time
of Use (ToU) Tariff/Night-time Concessional Tariff to encourage the HT consumers to use
more electricity during Off-Peak period. This is detailed as under:

1. Applicability

i. The ToD tariff shall be on optional basis and shall be available to the HT Supply (HT
Industry (including Are Furnace), HT NDS, Bulk Supply (other than Bulk (DS))
consumers who opt for the scheme.
ii. Smart Meter shall be the pre-requisite for availing ToD tariff. The same, if not installed
by the DISCOMs, can be installed by the Consumers as per CEA norms. The meters
should have appropriate registers to record the consumption during ToD hours for
commercial ToD accounting.
iii. It is further clarified that the Trivector meters are not smart meters. However, it is
possible to implement ToD Tariff with existing HT Trivector meters being used for AMR.
iv. In such cases, the requisite smart meter can be procured by the consumer from the
firms empanelled by the Nigam and handed over to the concerned SDO (OP) for
testing/sealing and installing. The XEN (OP) shall ensure that, in no case, the process
is delayed beyond ten days from the day (inclusive) the meter is handed over by a
consumer.
v. In case, meter installed is found to be non ToD compliant, no benefit will be allowed.
vi. The Discoms may extend the ToD Tariff to any other consumer category of consumer
receiving supply at HT level / with connected load/contract demand of 50 kW/KVA and
above.

465

vii. The consumers, desirous of availing the scheme as per the terms and conditions
mentioned hereinafter shall submit his application to the concerned SDO 'OP' who shall
forward the details to SE/Projects on the same day via email at
seprojects@uhbvn.org.in. SE/ Projects shall decide the applications and inform the
concerned consumer within three days of the date of application. A copy each of the
intimation to the consumer shall be sent to the Billing Agency and concerned
SDO(OP)/XEN (OP)/SE (OP). Complete category wise list of consumers who have opted
for the scheme shall also be sent to XEN (OP), SE (OP) and CE (Comml). It shall be the
responsibility of the XEN (OP) to ensure that the consumers who have opted for the
scheme are billed by the Billing Agency as per the ToD/Tou tariff.
viii. Once opting to avail the scheme, the consumer would continue to be charged ToD tariff
for the entire duration of the Scheme upto March, 2025. The billing under ToD tariff
shall commence from start of billing period immediately following the date of acceptance
of the application of the consumer.
ix. The scheme of ToD tariff would remain applicable from 01.11.2024 and remain
operative upto March, 2025 and shall terminate on 31 March, 2025 unless extended
by the Hon'ble Commission.
x. he ToD Tariff/Night time concessional Tariff, as given below, which shall be exclusive
of FSA, ED, M. Tax and Panchayat Tax would be applicable for the energy drawn during
off peak hours i.e. 22:00 to 05:30 hours over and above normal consumption in the
corresponding month of the preceding year.

per the below mentioned table:-

1.1   Further, in case of a connection where the period of one year from the date of
release of connection has yet not been completed and consequently the normal
consumption of the corresponding month of previous year is not available, the consumption
of billing month immediately preceding the month in which benefit of Night time
concessional tariff is to be availed will be considered as normal consumption subject to the
condition that same is found commensurate with his load/CD. In case, it is not, the
consumption as may be considered appropriate by the Committee of CE/Commercial and
SE/M&P shall be considered as normal consumption. In case of HT Supply consumers
running seasonal industries like rice shellers etc., the option of availing Night time
concessional tariff will not be available if the one year period from the date of connection
has not yet been completed.
  Provided, in case there has been an increase or decrease in load of a particular
consumer, the consumption figures shall be re-worked on prorata basis i.c. if load has been
enhanced by say 10%, the baseline consumption shall be escalated by 10% for the purpose
of working out the incremental / additional consumption.
1.2:   The scheme for ToD tariff mentioned above shall be subjected to following
conditions:
a) In case at any point of time the Discoms feel that further margins for accepting more
applications is not there, the Discoms will stop accepting new applications but the existing
beneficiaries would be allowed to continue availing concessional tariff.
b) In case of any force Majeure eventualities/ conditions i.e. unexpected fall in
availability/margins, more than expected additional load coming on the system etc., the
Discoms will stop/curtail the scheme by giving one week's notice to the beneficiaries.

2.   Apart from the above, the benefit of ToD/ToU tariff has also been extended to
Electric Vehicles Charging Station as detailed below:
"The energy charges as per TOD/TOU tariff shall also be applicable during the off-peak
demand period upto March) between 22:00 Hrs to 05:30 Hrs as applicable to the HT Supply
consumers on the total consumption, instead of incremental consumption, during the said
time period."
3.   The following data is required for onward submission to the HERC: -CE/SO
shall submit a monthly report with the analysis of the Load Curve of the State depicting
the data on different days and hours. The report should include the details of the demand
and supply of power with regard to the PPA's and actual power consumption in the State.
The data should be made to compare the before and after scenario in view of adoption of
ToD and its impact. Also, the accuracy of the data used to compute the period and time of
peak and non-peak hours should be submitted with facts to the Commission. It shall be
the duty of the Discoms along with SLDC to ensure accurate Demand Side Management
(DSM) so that benefit of ToD is optimized.

4.   Superintending Engineers (OP) shall hold meetings with industrial
associations to make them aware about benefits of the above scheme.
  The above instructions may be given wide publicity so that all eligible
consumers are made aware about the introduction of ToU/ToD tariff and be brought to the
notice of all concerned for strict and meticulous compliance.

Notes:
1. In case of Arc furnaces/ Steel Rolling Mills for supply at 33 kV and above, the HT
Industrial tariff at the corresponding voltage level shall be applicable. The tariff determined
in the table above for Arc Furnace taking supply at 11 kV voltage, is inclusive of surcharge.
However, the open access consumers bringing in power under Open Access Mechanism
shall also pay a surcharge of 30 Paisa/unit.
2. Fixed charges for HT supply and Bulk Supply category are in Rs. / kVA of Contract
Demand.
3. In case of Bulk Supply Consumers (other than Bulk Supply – DS), the fixed charges
are in Rs/kW of the connected load where contract demand is not sanctioned and in Rs.

474

/kVA of contract demand where contract demand is sanctioned.
4. Advocate’s Chamber, shall be levied a single rate (tariff) equivalent to CoS of LT
Supply (i.e. Rs.6.48) as determined in the present order. There shall be no demand / fixed
charges.
5. The electricity crematorium shall be levied a concessional tariff of Rs. 2.75 / Unit
(kVA or kWh). No demand charges shall be levied.
6. The schedule of tariff and charges does not include Electricity Duty, Municipal Tax,
Panchayat Tax (being levied as per the notifications issued by the State Government) and
FSA as per MYT Regulations in vogue.
7. Tariff for the eligible Gaushalas shall be Rs. 2.0 / kWh subject to payment of subsidy
by the State Government.
8. In case the State Government desires to extend concession including MMC/ subsidy
to any consumer category, the same shall be implementable subject to section 65 of the
Electricity Act, 2003.
9. The tariff for electricity supply to the EV Charging station in Haryana shall be a single
part tariff equivalent to the CoS of HT Supply (i.e. Rs. 6.12) and LT Supply (i.e. Rs. 6.48),
as determined in the present order. The off peak / night-time concession benefits shall also
be applicable. There shall be no fixed / demand charges.
10. In the case of the existing consumers above 50 kW upto 70 kW (LT) that has been
merged with HT Supply, the tariff shall be as per HT Supply. In the absence of a compatible
meter standard power factor of 0.90 may be used. However, the Discoms shall ensure that
a compatible meter of requisite accuracy is installed either by the Discoms or by the
consumers themselves within six months from this order. It is clarified that consumer will
not have the option to pick and choose. However, such consumers shall be given option
either to get the load reduced below 50 KW or convert to HT metering within one year.
11. The tariff for places of worship shall be a single part tariff equivalent to the Domestic
Supply tariff(s).
12. The charges, other than energy and demand charges determined in the present order,
for NDS category merged with HT / LT Supply shall be as per the charges applicable for
erstwhile HT / LT Industry. The Discoms are directed to file a comprehensive proposal for
amendment in general and miscellaneous charges as well as the relevant regulations such
as the Duty to Supply Regulations.
13. The Temporary Supply Tariff shall remain unchanged i.e. as per the Commission’s
tariff order for the FY 2021-22 i.e.,
“The tariff and charges for temporary supply shall be 1.2 times fixed charges and
1.5 times the energy charges of the relevant category for which temporary supply
has been sought. While releasing electric supply on temporary basis, the DISCOMs
must mention the period for which temporary supply has been sought and given. In
case the said period gets extended for whatever reasons, the multiplication factor
for both fixed charges and energy charges shall be 2 times.
The Commission has also clarified in its order dated 31.03.2022 in case No.
HERC/RA-08 of 2021 that 2 times charges are to be levied from the extension of
period of the said connection.”
14. The AP Supply tariff shall be Rs. 6.48 / kWh for metered supply and BHP (in the case
of flat rate shall be converted to kW and units worked out by applying the average running

tariff provided advance subsidy, in the beginning of each quarter is paid by the State
Government to the Discoms, as per Section 65 of the Electricity Act, 2003.

16.5 Waiving of Monthly Minimum Charges (MMC) for Domestic Consumers-
SOP thereof. (Sales Instructions No. U-01/2025)

477

Please refer to Nigam's Sales Circular No. U-16/2024 dated 19.06.2024, regarding the
waiver of Monthly Minimum Charges (MMC) for domestic consumer with a sanctioned load
of upto 2kW and a monthly consumption of 100 units or less.
To ensure the smooth implementation of this Government Scheme, the following Standard
Operating Procedure (SOP) has been established:

1. Standard MIS Design:
 SE/IT, in consultation with FA/HQ, UHBVN, Panchkula, will design the Standard
MIS:
 The designed MIS must be audited by the Chief Auditor, UHBVN before
implementation.

2. Monthly Reporting:
 SE/IT will access the system to extract the required MIS monthly and send the same
to FA/HQ. The MIS reports shall also be made available to field offices for doing needful.
 Claims for reimbursement will be raised by FA/HQ to the Government of Haryana in
a timely manner

3. Further Audits:
 Chief Auditor will ensure additional audits of data as necessary at any subsequent
stage. All the required changes in MIS will be made by SE/IT.

4. Consumer Billing Transparency:
 SE/IT, UHBVN will ensure the implementation of clause 2.3 (xvii) of SoP on subsidy
accounting and payment i.e. "DISCOMs shall mention both per unit full cost tariff and
subsidy provided by the State Government separately on the consumer bills where any type
of concession/subsidy is involved in consumer billing.

5. Clubbing Of Loads in the same premises:

 Operation wing shall identify premises where multiple connections are provided
which otherwise are not eligible for multiple connections in accordance with the provision
of HERC Duty to Supply Regulation, 2016, as amended from time to time (Sales Circular
No. U-09/2020).
In such premises, the enforcement of the "Clubbing of Load" provision shall be meticulously
examined and implemented as applicable.

6. Replacement of Defective / Damaged Meters
 Defective or damaged energy meters shall be replaced immediately. Operation Sub-
Division shall ensure accurate recording of energy consumption for beneficiaries under the
Waiver of MMC scheme through the energy meter.

16.6 Standard Operating Procedure for Supply of Green Power (Solar or Non-
Solar) in Haryana under ‘Green Energy Premium’ tariff mechanism (Sales Instruction
No. U-01/2022)

Hon’ble HERC in its Tariff order dated 30.03.2022 has introduced “Green Energy Premium”
as the charge which consumers opting for green energy will have to pay to the Discoms @
Rs. 2/unit for Solar energy and Rs. 1/unit for Non-Solar energy, over and above the normal
tariff applicable for the respective consumer category to which such consumer belongs.
  Such consumer may, if so desires, opt for entering into a contract with the
Discoms for supply of 100% green power (Solar or Non-Solar) to them. The Discoms shall
procure green energy (Solar or Non-Solar, as per the requirement of the consumers) and
issue a monthly certificate to the “obligated embedded consumer” stating the quantum of
renewable energy (Solar or Non-Solar) supplied, which will count towards their RPO
obligations as well.
  As such, the detailed procedure for submission of application by consumer
and for levy of ‘Green Energy Premium’ to the consumer opting for 100% Renewable Energy
is as under:-
1. All the applicants who are interested in availing 100% Green Energy from UHBVN
shall submit the application as per format enclosed as Annexure I.
2. Along with the application, the applicant shall submit an undertaking as per the
format enclosed as Annexure II.
3. The Tenure for availing the 100% Green Power shall be at least one complete billing
cycle or any such billing cycle specified by the applicant in its application and no revision
will be accepted by UHBVN w.r.t the said period.
4. The applicant shall submit the application to the office of SE/Projects either in hard

479

copy or through email id- seprojects@uhbvn.org.in
5. The Green Energy Premium of Rs. 2/unit for Solar and Rs. 1/unit for Non-Solar,
which are over and above the normal tariff of respective category, will be levied to the
consumers (as per the notification of HERC) opting for 100% Green energy. This shall
however, be ensured by SE/Projects.
6. The application will be scrutinized by SE/Projects, UHBVN and as per the eligibility
of the same, it will be allowed by him with intimation to HPPC and to the applicant.
7. Green Energy Premium so levied in the energy bills shall also be depicted separately
in the bills for which provisions in the existing bill format shall be ensured by SE/Projects,
UHBVN.
  The Certificate ( Annexure III) regarding 100% Green Energy Consumption
shall be issued by SE/Projects, UHBVN to the applicant along with the monthly energy bill
of the consumer.

16.9 Charges to be recovered from Northern Railways (Deemed Distribution
Licensee).( Sales Circular No. U-17/2020)

The Petition No. HERC/PRO-11 of 2017 was filed before Hon’ble HERC seeking clarification
on various applicable charges under Clause 19, 20, 21, 22, 23, 24, 57, 58 and 59 of
Haryana Electricity Regulatory Commission (Terms and conditions for grant of connectivity
and open access for intra State transmission and distribution system) Regulations, 2012
(No. 25/HERC/2012 dated 11.01.2012) to be levied on Northern Railways (Deemed

482

Distribution Licensee) for availing medium term open access.
  The Hon’ble Commission has passed a final order dated 17.06.2020 (Copy
attached) and decided the charges applicable / recoverable from Northern Railways. The
details are as under:-

1. Wheeling Charges
Hon’ble Commission observed that Northern Railway is not an embedded Open Access
Consumer but incidentally Northern Railway as a medium term Open Access Consumer is
using the distribution system of UHBVN, so wheeling charges determined by the
commission are not recoverable from Northern Railway. However, Northern Railway is liable
to bear distribution system network cost as determined by the Commission for the relevant
year i.e. Rs. 0.47 per Unit for FY 2020-21 besides intra State transmission loss. The
distribution system network cost has been determined in the ARR/Tariff order of HVPNL
(STU).
2. Cross Subsidy Surcharge (CSS)
HERC OA Regulations provides that cross subsidy surcharge shall also be payable by such
open access consumer who receives supply of electricity from a person other than the
distribution licensee in whose area of supply he is located, irrespective of whether he avails
such supply through transmission/distribution network of the licensee or not.
As Northern railway is using the network of the licensee(s), so the CSS determined by the
Commission in its order on true- up for the FY 2018-19, annual (mid-year) performance
review for the FY 2019-20, aggregate revenue requirement of UHBVNL and DHBVNL for the
MYT control period 2020-21 TO FY 2024-2025 and distribution & retail supply tariff for the
FY 2020-21, shall be applicable to the Northern Railway.
3. Additional Surcharge
Additional surcharge shall be applicable to Northern Railway as determined by the
Commission for relevant year.
4. Charges for Standby Power
The Nigam can charge 1.5 times the tariff (Fixed + Energy) for temporary supply (short
duration) as well as FSA and Peak Load Exemption Charges (PLEC) if applicable. In the
case of Northern Railway (taking supply at say 66 or 132 kV) this would work out in excess
of Rs. 11 / kWh without including FSA and PLEC. Hence, any further deterrence in the
shape of penalty is not required.
5. Imbalance Charges
Imbalances / deviations shall be settled as per guidelines of HERC Regulations, 2019
(Deviation Settlement & Mechanism dated 29th April, 2019) instead of HERC Open Access
Regulations, 2012 amended from time to time. These charges are in addition to charges
levied by HVPNL/SLDC. The above charges shall be applicable with retrospective effect till
such time the Northern Railway fulfils all the terms and condition including payment of
fees specified for a distribution licensee / deemed to be distribution licensee.

16.11 Peak load exemption charges (PLEC). (Sales Circular No. U- 21 /2018)

Please refer to clause 6 of sales circular No. U-17/2014 dated 03.04.2014 vide which it has
been directed that PLEC shall not be applicable on those industrial consumers who are
being supplied from rural agriculture or rural domestic feeders as they are already being
given heavily curtailed supply.
   Now the matter has been considered and clarified that the PLEC shall also be
levied on RDS feeders getting 24 hours supply on the pattern of urban and industrial /
independent feeders.
  Further, the peak load exemption charges be levied as per sales circular No.
U-39 / 2014.
All relevant sales circulars are amended to the above extent only.

15.12 Clarification on tariff applicable to mushroom farming / tissue culture etc.(
Sales Instruction No. U-04/2018)

Please refer to sales circular No. U-02/2001, the mushroom cultivation is covered under
DS tariff or Non-domestic tariff depending upon whether the cultivation is being done in
one or two rooms of a domestic premises or NDS premises/area respectively. Subsequently,
some connections for mushroom cultivation were released under LT industrial category
also.
2.  A number of representations were received by the Dept. Of Agriculture, GoH from
persons engaged in mushroom cultivation for charging AP tariff instead of
DS/NDS/industrial tariff. The matter was taken up by the Dept. of Agriculture with Dept.
of Power. It was intimated by the then Principal Secretary/Power, GoH, vide D.O. No.
PS/Additional.C.S-2013/Ch-7/SS-403 /Horticulture /Loose /2/CGM/C-I Chandigarh,
dated the 31st July, 2013 and again vide D.O. No. PS/PR Secretary (Power)/Ch-15/SS-
403/Horticulture/Loose/2/CGM/C-I Chandigarh, dated the 19.08.2014 to then Principal
Secretary/ Agriculture Dept. GoH, to take up the matter with the State Government for its
concurrence to pay subsidy to compensate the Discom for the revenue loss on account of
levy of subsidized AP tariff to mushroom cultivation instead of industrial/NDS tariff being
levied. However, State Govt. so far has not given its concurrence for applying AP tariff to
mushroom cultivation and pay additional subsidy to the Discoms for the revenue loss on
account of change of tariff presently being charged i.e. DS/NDS/industrial to AP tariff.
3.  Further it is intimated that HERC in case no HERC/PRO-35 of 2013, wherein, the
Petitioner had pleaded for levy of subsidized AP tariff for tissue culture, had decided vide
its interim order dated 20.10.2014 to obtain the consent of State Government for

491

admissibility of subsidized AP tariff to tissue culture and payment of subsidy. Matter was
accordingly taken up with the then ACS /Power and it was intimated to HERC, with the
concurrence of ACS /Power, vide letter dated 01.01.2015 that the subsidised AP tariff
should only be provided to the activities where tubewells or pumpsets are used for irrigating
fields and for plantation purposes and that the other Horticulture activities i.e. Tissue
Culture Lab etc. are commercial in nature and Industrial/NDS tariff is rightly chargeable.
Mushroom cultivation also falls in the same category.
4.  It is, therefore, clear that mushroom cultivation is not covered under Schedule of
Agriculture Tubewell/ Lift Irrigation/ MITC Supply for which AP tariff is applicable as it
does not involve use of tube wells/pump sets for irrigating fields or for plantation in any
manner. Mushroom cultivation, on the other hand, involves use of high technology with
extensive use of ACs, Blower, Heaters etc for cultivation and, therefore, should be covered
under Industrial category only instead of DS/NDS/ Industrial as at present.
5.  In view of above, it has been decided that all electrical connections for mushroom
cultivation henceforth shall be covered under industrial category and any existing
connection presently under any other category should immediately be changed to industrial
category. The consumer will not be required to pay any charges for effecting this change.
  All related sales circulars/instructions are superseded.

16.13 Schedule of Tariff for FY 2013-14 for supply for electricity by
Distribution Licensees i.e. UHBVNL and DHBVNL in Haryana (Sales Instruction No. U-
08/2017)

Please refer to S.I. No. U-6/2017 dated 14.06.2017 wherein clarification in
respect of clause -2, of Non-Domestic Supply, of S.C. No. U-30/2013 was issued as under;-
“Now, Clause-2 – Non-Domestic Supply, it is clarified that all Non-Agriculture category
consumers which are not covered under Domestic/ Industrial/ Bulk Supply/ Public Water
Works/ MITC/ Street Light/ Traction/DMRC shall be considered Non-Domestic Supply
category consumers.”
2.  It has been observed by Hon’ble HERC vide memo no. 1309-10/HERC/Tariff
dated 13.07.2017 that Temporary Metered Supply, Lift Irrigation and Independent
Hoarding/ Decorative Lighting are also required to be excluded from Non-Domestic Supply.
  In view of the above observation of the Hon’ble Commission, the clarification
in respect of Non-Domestic Supply Schedule of tariff issued vide S.I. No. U-06/2017 is
amended to read as under:-
  Regarding clause-2, Non-Domestic Supply of Schedule of tariff, it is clarified
that all Non-Agriculture category consumers which are not covered under Domestic/
Industrial/ Bulk Supply/ Public Water Works/ MITC/ Street Light/ Traction/
DMRC/Temporary Metered Supply/ Lift Irrigation and Independent Hoarding/ Decorative
Lighting shall be considered Non-Domestic Supply category consumers.
3.  Sales Circular No. U-30/2013 stands amended to this extent and Sales
Instruction No. U-06/2017 stands superseded

1. DOMESTIC SUPPLY (DS)
(i) Applicability
Applicable to consumers for lights, fans, domestic pumping sets, lifts, fire hydrants, and
house-hold appliances in the following premises:-

(b) Group housing societies other than those covered under HERC (Single Point Supply
to Employers’ Colonies, Group Housing Societies and Residential or Commercial cum
Residential Complexes of Developers) Regulations, 2013 (hereinafter referred to as
Single Point Supply Regulations). In case of Group Housing Societies covered under
Single Point Supply Regulations and opting for option-2, individual connections to
residents of such Group Housing Societies shall also be covered under Domestic
Supply Schedule subject to the conditions in the said Regulations
(c) Hostel of Educational Institutions (including Mess/ Canteen),
(d) Working Women's hostels run by Red Cross and Social Welfare Department,
(e)  Anganwadi Workers’ training Centres set up by Indian Council for Child Welfare,
(f) Places of public worship such as Mandirs, Masjids, Churches, Gurdwaras,
(g) Village Chaupal owned by Gram Panchayat / Communities.

NOTES
i) Private dwelling, in which space is occasionally used for the conduct of business by
a person residing therein, shall also be served under this tariff.
ii) Where a portion of the dwelling is used regularly for the conduct of a business, the
consumption in that portion shall be separately metered and billed under the appropriate
Non-Domestic tariff or Industrial power supply tariff. If separate meters are not provided,
the entire supply will be classified under Non-Domestic supply or industrial power supply
tariff as applicable.
iii) Resale of energy is strictly prohibited except where necessary permission/exemption
is granted by Haryana Electricity Regulatory Commission.
iv) A hostel shall be considered as one unit and billed without compounding. The supply
for residential quarters/flats attached to the educational institutions for staff-members
shall also be considered as one unit and billed without compounding.
v) Consumption of Street lighting in Group Housing Societies, other than those covered
under Bulk Supply (Domestic) Schedule, shall be billed at Domestic tariff.
